# pixi-silk

> Smooth vector graphics for PixiJS v8. pixi-silk draws shapes as exact signed distance fields, so every edge is anti-aliased per pixel. Edges stay smooth at any zoom, rotation and device pixel ratio, without MSAA, and each object is one draw call.

pixi-silk 0.1.0 is an MIT-licensed TypeScript library. It needs pixi.js ^8 (peer dependency) and WebGL2.
- `SilkGraphics` is a display object with a Graphics-like API. It draws rects and squircles (per-corner radii), circles, ellipses, arcs, sectors, lines, polylines (smoothed or tapered), Bezier paths (stroke only), chart areas, hearts, stars, polygons and rounded triangles.
- Paint: colours, gradients (linear, radial, conic, along the path), a gaussian `blur` for glows and soft shadows, dashes and dots. Gradients mix in OKLab and are dithered. Strokes align inside, center or outside.
- `createSilkApp` creates a Pixi Application whose canvas maps 1:1 to device pixels, even at fractional ratios. It follows DPR changes, uses no MSAA and renders filters at screen resolution.
- Also: transforms (save, restore, translate, rotate, scale), hit testing against the real shapes, and motion helpers (damp, Spring, ease).
- Limits: WebGL2 only, no WebGPU yet. Free-form paths are stroke-only. Joins are always round.

Site: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev
Repository: https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-silk
Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/pixi-silk

This file contains the complete documentation: every guide (live demos are inlined as their TypeScript source), the API reference and the FAQ.

## Quick start

```bash
npm install pixi-silk pixi.js
```

```ts
import { createSilkApp, SilkGraphics, conic, vertical } from 'pixi-silk';

const { app } = await createSilkApp({ parent: document.getElementById('stage')!, background: 0x000000 });
const g = new SilkGraphics();

g.roundRect(10, 10, 340, 140, 22, 0.6).fill(0x1c1c1e);                        // squircle card
g.arcSweep(80, 80, 44, -Math.PI / 2, Math.PI * 1.5)
    .stroke({ width: 12, cap: 'round', gradient: conic([0x30d158, 0xffd60a, 0xff453a]) });
g.area([120, 100, 170, 80, 220, 92, 270, 60, 320, 70], 130, { smooth: 'monotone' })
    .fill(vertical([[0, 0xff9f0a, 0.8], [1, 0xff9f0a, 0]]))
    .stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xff9f0a, cap: 'round' });
app.stage.addChild(g);
```

---

# Getting started

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/getting-started/
Section: Learn

> Install pixi-silk next to pixi.js v8, create an app with createSilkApp and draw a squircle card, a gradient gauge and an area chart with SilkGraphics.

pixi-silk adds `SilkGraphics`, a PixiJS v8 display object with an API close to `Graphics`. You
add it to the stage like any other container.

Live demo `quick-start` (source):

```ts
import { conic, SilkGraphics, vertical } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

const GAUGE = conic([0x30d158, 0xffd60a, 0xff453a]);
const FILL = vertical(
    [
        [0, 0xff9f0a, 0.8],
        [1, 0xff9f0a, 0],
    ],
    { easing: 'smooth' },
);

export default defineDemo({
    size: [360, 160],
    controls: {
        progress: { type: 'range', label: 'progress', min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01, value: 0.72 },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            const wave = [120, 100, 170, 80, 220, 92, 270, 60, 320, 70].map((v, i) =>
                i % 2 ? v + Math.sin(t + i) * 6 : v,
            );

            g.clear();
            g.roundRect(10, 10, 340, 140, 22, 0.6).fill(0x1c1c1e); // squircle card
            g.arcSweep(80, 80, 44, -Math.PI / 2, Math.PI * 2).stroke({ width: 12, color: 0x2c2c2e });
            g.arcSweep(80, 80, 44, -Math.PI / 2, Math.PI * 2 * params.progress).stroke({
                width: 12,
                cap: 'round',
                gradient: GAUGE,
            }); // gauge follows the arc
            g.area(wave, 130, { smooth: 'monotone' })
                .fill(FILL) // chart fill ...
                .stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xff9f0a, cap: 'round' }); // ... and its top line
        });
    },
});
```

## Install

```bash
npm install pixi-silk pixi.js
```

`pixi.js` 8.6 or newer is a peer dependency, so your app owns the renderer. The package is ESM
with TypeScript declarations and has no side effects, so a bundler keeps only what you import.

## Create the app

```ts

const { app } = await createSilkApp({
    parent: document.getElementById('stage')!, // the canvas fills this element
    background: 0x000000,
});
```

`createSilkApp` wraps `new Application()` and `app.init()`. It turns MSAA off, sizes the canvas
so one canvas pixel is one device pixel, and follows changes of the device pixel ratio. You can
keep your own `Application` instead. [Resolution](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/resolution/) lists the settings that matter.

## Draw

Shape methods add to the active path. `fill()` and `stroke()` paint it, and every call chains.

```ts

const GAUGE = conic([0x30d158, 0xffd60a, 0xff453a]); // spans the arc it is drawn on
const g = new SilkGraphics();

g.roundRect(10, 10, 340, 140, 22, 0.6).fill(0x1c1c1e); // radius 22, squircle smoothing 0.6
g.arcSweep(80, 80, 44, -Math.PI / 2, Math.PI * 1.5).stroke({ width: 12, cap: 'round', gradient: GAUGE });
g.area([120, 100, 170, 80, 220, 92, 270, 60, 320, 70], 130, { smooth: 'monotone' })
    .fill(vertical([[0, 0xff9f0a, 0.8], [1, 0xff9f0a, 0]]))
    .stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xff9f0a, cap: 'round' }); // a stroke right after a fill draws the top line

app.stage.addChild(g);
```

The card is a squircle, the gauge is one arc with a conic gradient along it, and the chart is a
smoothed area with a fading fill.

## Animate

Redraw every frame. `clear()` keeps the GPU buffers, so a rebuild only rewrites numbers.

```ts
app.ticker.add((ticker) => {
    const t = ticker.lastTime / 1000;

    g.clear();
    g.arcSweep(80, 80, 44, -Math.PI / 2, Math.PI * 2 * (0.5 + 0.4 * Math.sin(t)))
        .stroke({ width: 12, cap: 'round', gradient: GAUGE });
});
```

Create gradients once and reuse them. Ramps with the same stops share one row of the gradient
atlas, and a reused object skips parsing the stops again.

## What it does differently

`Graphics` turns shapes into triangles when you draw, and only MSAA smooths their edges.
`SilkGraphics` draws each shape as a quad. The fragment shader evaluates the shape's exact
distance function at every pixel and turns the distance into coverage.

Two things follow from that. Edges stay sharp at any zoom and in filters and render textures,
because nothing was tessellated. And one `SilkGraphics` renders in one instanced draw call,
whatever it holds. Call `enableSilkBatching()` before you create objects to draw runs of them in
one call too. [Anti-aliasing compared](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/anti-aliasing-compared/) sets this against MSAA,
`@pixi/graphics-smooth` and supersampling, and [How it works](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/how-it-works/) walks
through the shader.

It renders with WebGL2 by default. [Renderers](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/renderers/) shows how to turn on WebGPU.

## Where it stops

| You want | Use |
|---|---|
| Texture or pattern fills | a Pixi `Sprite` or `TilingSprite` |
| A whole SVG file | Pixi's `Graphics.svg()`. `svgPath(d)` takes one path's `d` attribute |
| Text | `SilkText` from `pixi-silk/text`, a separate entry point |

## Where next

- [Choose an entry point](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/choose-an-entry-point/) lists what each import holds.
- [Migrating from Graphics](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/migrating-from-graphics/) maps your existing calls.
- [Your first widget](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/first-widget/) builds a button with a glow, hover and press.
- [Shapes](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/shapes/) lists every primitive.

# Migrating from Graphics

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/migrating-from-graphics/
Section: Learn

> SilkGraphics follows the PixiJS v8 Graphics API: shapes on a path, fill and stroke, transforms. See what carries over, what differs and what to add.

Most `Graphics` code runs after you rename the class.

Live demo `versus` (source):

```ts
import { Container, Graphics, Text } from 'pixi.js';
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// Left: Pixi v8 Graphics (tessellated, no MSAA). Right: SilkGraphics (distance fields).
export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 240],
    controls: {
        zoom: { type: 'range', label: 'zoom', min: 1, max: 6, step: 0.01, value: 1 },
        spin: { type: 'toggle', label: 'rotate', value: true },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const sides = [new Container(), new Container()];
        const pixi = new Graphics();
        const silk = new SilkGraphics();

        sides[0].addChild(pixi);
        sides[1].addChild(silk);
        sides.forEach((side, i) => {
            const mask = new Graphics().rect(i * 240, 0, 240, 240).fill(0xffffff);
            const label = new Text({
                text: i ? 'SilkGraphics' : 'Graphics',
                style: { fill: 0x8e8e93, fontSize: 12, fontFamily: 'system-ui' },
            });

            label.position.set(i * 240 + 12, 10);
            side.mask = mask;
            stage.addChild(side, mask, label);
        });
        let angle = 0;

        tick((_t, dt) => {
            if (params.spin) angle += dt * 0.15;
            for (const [i, side] of sides.entries()) {
                side.pivot.set(120, 130);
                side.position.set(i * 240 + 120, 130);
                side.scale.set(params.zoom);
                side.rotation = angle;
            }
            for (const g of [pixi, silk]) {
                g.clear();
                g.circle(120, 130, 62).stroke({ width: 3, color: 0x64d2ff });
                g.roundRect(70, 90, 100, 80, 24).stroke({ width: 1, color: 0xffffff });
                g.circle(120, 130, 18).fill(0xff375f);
                for (let k = 0; k < 6; k++)
                    g.moveTo(40, 60 + k * 3)
                        .lineTo(200, 64 + k * 5)
                        .stroke({ width: 0.6, color: 0xffd60a });
            }
        });
    },
});
```

```diff
- const g = new Graphics();
+ const g = new SilkGraphics();
  g.roundRect(0, 0, 200, 80, 16).fill(0x1c1c1e).stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xffffff });
  g.circle(40, 40, 12).fill({ color: 0xff375f, alpha: 0.8 });
  g.moveTo(0, 100).lineTo(200, 120).stroke({ width: 1, color: 0xffffff });
```

The shapes go on the active path as before, and `fill()` and `stroke()` paint them. A
`stroke()` right after a `fill()` strokes the same shapes.

## What carries over

| Graphics | SilkGraphics |
|---|---|
| `rect`, `roundRect`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `poly`, `regularPoly` | the same calls |
| `moveTo`, `lineTo`, `quadraticCurveTo`, `bezierCurveTo`, `arc`, `closePath`, `beginPath` | the same calls |
| `fill(color)`, `fill({ color, alpha })` | the same, plus `gradient`, `blur` and `spread` |
| `stroke({ width, color, alpha, alignment, cap, join, miterLimit })` | the same. `alignment` also takes `'inside'`, `'center'` and `'outside'` |
| `save`, `restore`, `translateTransform`, `rotateTransform`, `scaleTransform`, `setTransform`, `resetTransform` | the same calls |
| `clear()` | the same, and it keeps the GPU buffers for the next frame |

It is a regular display object. Position it, mask it, filter it or render it into a texture. Set
`eventMode` to get pointer events, and hit tests use the real shape, so a ring is hollow.

## What differs

| Graphics | SilkGraphics |
|---|---|
| holes with `cut()` | a free path fills even-odd, so an inner subpath is a hole. `cut()` does not exist |
| `texture` fills | not supported. Use gradients, or a Sprite |
| `svg(markup)` parses a whole SVG | `svgPath(d)` takes one path's `d` attribute |
| batched with other Graphics | one draw call per object, or per run of objects after `enableSilkBatching()` |
| `GraphicsContext` shared between objects | no shared context. Redraw each object, it is cheap |

## What to add

These have no `Graphics` equivalent.

```ts
g.roundRect(0, 0, 160, 96, [24, 24, 8, 8], 0.6).fill(0x2c2c2e); // per-corner radii, squircle smoothing
g.arcSweep(200, 48, 36, -Math.PI / 2, Math.PI).stroke({ width: 10, cap: 'round', color: 0x30d158 });
g.polyline([0, 140, 60, 120, 120, 150, 180, 110], { smooth: 'monotone' }).stroke({ width: [2, 8], color: 0x0a84ff });
g.circle(260, 140, 20).fill({ color: 0xff9f0a, blur: 12 }); // a glow, no filter
g.rect(300, 110, 60, 60).stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xffffff, dash: [6, 4] });
```

That is a squircle card with two rounded and two tighter corners, a gauge arc, a smoothed line
that tapers from 2 to 8 px, a blurred dot and a dashed square. [Shapes](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/shapes/),
[Lines & paths](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/lines-and-paths/) and [Strokes & dashes](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/strokes-and-dashes/) cover
each call.

## Migrate one screen at a time

`Graphics` and `SilkGraphics` sit in the same scene. Swap the objects that show edges first:
large curves, thin lines and anything under a zooming camera or a filter. Leave texture fills and
SVG files on `Graphics`.

# Choose an entry point

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/choose-an-entry-point/
Section: Learn

> pixi-silk ships one entry point per feature. See what the root import holds, what lives under ui, text, layout, glass, glow and webgpu, and when to import each.

The root import `pixi-silk` holds the drawing core. Everything else has its own entry point, so
an app that only draws shapes never downloads the text renderer or the editor widgets.

```ts
```

The UI widgets, text, layout, glass, glow and the WebGPU shader are not in the root import. An

## Core

| Import | What it holds | Import it when |
|---|---|---|
| `pixi-silk` | `SilkGraphics`, gradients (`linear`, `radial`, `conic`, `along`, `mesh`), `createSilkApp`, `enableSilkBatching`, `Spring`, `damp`, `ease`, colour and curve helpers | always |
| `pixi-silk/webgpu` | `enableWebGPU()`, the WGSL shader | you create your own Pixi app with WebGPU. See [Renderers](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/renderers/) |
| `pixi-silk/signal` | `signal`, `computed`, `watch`, `batch` | you read or write widget state, which is kept in signals |

## Text, layout and effects

| Import | What it holds | Import it when |
|---|---|---|
| `pixi-silk/text` | `SilkText`, `silkLabel`, `SdfAtlas`, text layout and caret helpers | you draw labels. See [Text](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/text/) |
| `pixi-silk/layout` | `LayoutNode`, a flex layout engine with no Pixi in it | you lay out boxes in a worker, a test or a server. See [Layout engine](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/layout-engine/) |
| `pixi-silk/ui/layout` | `SmartContainer`, `FlexContainer`, `simulateViewport`, `layoutDebug` | you place Pixi containers on a responsive screen. See [Layout](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/layout/) |
| `pixi-silk/glass` | `Glass`, `GlassFilter` | you want frosted panels. See [Glass & glow](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glass-and-glow/) |
| `pixi-silk/glow` | `Glow`, `Aurora`, `neon`, `halo`, `shadowStack`, light rays | you want neon, halos or light beams |

## Interface widgets

| Import | What it holds | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `pixi-silk/ui/button` | `SilkButton` | [Radial menus & buttons](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/radial-menus-and-buttons/) |
| `pixi-silk/ui/radial` | `RadialMenu`, `bindRadialTrigger` | [Radial menus & buttons](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/radial-menus-and-buttons/) |
| `pixi-silk/ui/dock` | `ButtonDock` | [Radial menus and buttons](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/radial-menus-and-buttons/) |
| `pixi-silk/ui/odometer` | `Odometer` | [Interaction and motion](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/interaction-and-motion/) |
| `pixi-silk/ui/pill` | `ValuePill` | [Gizmos and selection](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/gizmos-and-selection/) |
| `pixi-silk/ui/gesture` | `trackGesture` | [Interaction & motion](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/interaction-and-motion/) |
| `pixi-silk/ui/textedit` | `TextEditor` | [Editing text](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/editing-text/) |

## Everything at once

`pixi-silk/ui` re-exports every widget above, plus `pixi-silk/selection`, `pixi-silk/history` and
`pixi-silk/path`. It is handy in a prototype. In an app, import from the widget's own path so the
bundle holds only the widgets you use.

The package has no side effects, so a bundler drops the widgets you do not use from either
import. The narrow paths make that independent of how well your bundler tree-shakes.

---

# Your first widget

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/first-widget/
Section: Learn

> Build a pill button with SilkGraphics: a soft glow from a blurred fill, springs for hover and press, and a SilkText label. Then compare it with SilkButton.

This tutorial builds a pill button that glows, brightens on hover and dips when pressed. It uses
`SilkGraphics` for the shape and the glow, two springs for motion and `SilkText` for the label.

## Draw the button

A button is a container with a graphics object and a label in it. The pivot sits at the centre,
so the press can scale it in place. `paint()` redraws the shape for a hover and a press amount
from 0 to 1.

```ts

const W = 180;
const H = 56;
const button = new Container();
const shape = new SilkGraphics();
const label = new SilkText({ text: 'Play', fontSize: 20, fontWeight: 600, fill: 0xffffff, anchor: 0.5 });

label.position.set(W / 2, H / 2);
button.addChild(shape, label);
button.pivot.set(W / 2, H / 2);
button.position.set(200, 120);
app.stage.addChild(button);

function paint(hover: number, press: number) {
    shape.clear();
    shape.pill(0, 0, W, H).fill({ color: 0x0a84ff, alpha: 0.4 + 0.5 * hover, blur: 10 + 8 * hover, spread: 2, blend: 'add' });
    shape.pill(0, 0, W, H).fill(press > 0.5 ? 0x0060df : 0x0a84ff);
}

paint(0, 0);
```

`SilkText` comes from `pixi-silk/text`, a separate entry point. Its glyphs are distance fields
too, so the label stays sharp when the button scales.

## The glow

`paint()` draws the pill twice. The first copy is the glow: `blur` softens it, `spread` grows it
before the blur so it keeps a bright core, and `blend: 'add'` brightens the background instead of
covering it. Both pills render in the object's one draw call, with no filter and no extra texture.

## Add hover and press

`Spring` from the root import moves a value towards a target. This function wires pointer events
to two springs and repaints while they move.

```ts

export function animate(button: Container, paint: (hover: number, press: number) => void, ticker: Ticker) {
    const hover = new Spring(0, 300, 30); // value, stiffness, damping
    const press = new Spring(0, 700, 32);

    button.eventMode = 'static';
    button.cursor = 'pointer';
    button.on('pointerover', () => (hover.target = 1));
    button.on('pointerout', () => {
        hover.target = 0;
        press.target = 0;
    });
    button.on('pointerdown', () => (press.target = 1));
    button.on('pointerup', () => {
        press.target = 0;
        console.log('pressed');
    });

    ticker.add((t) => {
        if (hover.settled && press.settled) return;
        const h = hover.step(t.deltaMS / 1000);
        const p = press.step(t.deltaMS / 1000);

        paint(h, p);
        button.scale.set(1 - 0.05 * p);
    });
}
```

Call `animate(button, paint, app.ticker)`. Hovering raises the glow over a few frames. Pressing
shrinks the button by 5% and darkens it, and releasing springs it back. The ticker skips the repaint once both springs rest.

Pointer events test the pill shape, not a bounding box, so the corners outside the rounded ends
do not react.

## The ready-made button

`SilkButton` from `pixi-silk/ui/button` does all of this and handles the cases an app needs.

```ts

const play = new SilkButton({ label: 'Play', width: 180, height: 56, onPress: () => console.log('pressed') });

play.position.set(200, 200);
app.stage.addChild(play);
```

It ignores input while it animates in or out, while it is disabled and while `state.busy` shows
a spinner. A press that slides off still counts when it is released close by, and `holdMs` adds a
long press. Write your own button when you need a look it does not draw, and use `SilkButton` for
the input rules.

## Where next

- [Glass & glow](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glass-and-glow/) has a glowing button demo and the `pixi-silk/glow` recipes.
- [Radial menus & buttons](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/radial-menus-and-buttons/) lists every `SilkButton` option.
- [Interaction & motion](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/interaction-and-motion/) covers hit testing and springs.

# Your first editor canvas

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/first-editor-canvas/
Section: Learn

> Build an editor canvas in PixiJS v8 with the pixi-silk editor kit: a camera that pans and zooms, a grid, a selection store, outlines and a transform gizmo.

This tutorial builds the core of a design tool canvas: a camera that pans and zooms, a grid,
click to select and a gizmo that moves the selected layer.

> **NOTE**
> Experimental in 1.0: the API may change in a minor release.

Live demo `editor-canvas` (source):

```ts
import { Container } from 'pixi.js';
import { linear, SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { bindHistoryKeys, History, recordGizmo } from 'pixi-silk/history';
import { bindGizmo, bindMeasure, bindOutline, Selection } from 'pixi-silk/selection';
import { watch } from 'pixi-silk/signal';
import { SilkText, silkLabel } from 'pixi-silk/text';
import { Camera, ZoomControl } from 'pixi-silk/ui/camera';
import { TransformGizmo } from 'pixi-silk/ui/gizmo';
import { altDown } from 'pixi-silk/ui/keys';
import { Measure } from 'pixi-silk/ui/measure';
import { SelectionOutline } from 'pixi-silk/ui/outline';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// Scroll to pan, pinch or ctrl + scroll to zoom, right drag or Space + drag to pan.
// Click a layer to select it, Shift + click to add more. Hover another to measure the distance
// to it. Drag the arrows to move a layer, cmd or ctrl + Z undoes and Shift + cmd + Z redoes.
export default defineDemo({
    size: [760, 480],
    background: 0x151517,
    touchAction: 'none',
    ownsCamera: true,
    controls: {
        redlines: { type: 'select', label: 'redlines', options: ['on hover', 'with Alt'], value: 'on hover' },
    },
    setup({ silk, params }) {
        const app = silk.app;
        const world = new Container();
        const overlay = new Container();
        const camera = new Camera({ world, element: app.canvas });
        const hover = new SelectionOutline({ ticker: app.ticker });
        const outline = new SelectionOutline({ ticker: app.ticker });
        const gizmo = new TransformGizmo({ ticker: app.ticker });
        // SilkText labels: distance fields stay sharp at any zoom
        const label = silkLabel();
        const measure = new Measure({ space: world, ticker: app.ticker, label });
        const zoom = new ZoomControl(camera, { label });
        // one selection store drives the outlines, the gizmo and the redlines
        const selection = new Selection<Container>();
        const history = new History();

        gizmo.state.mode.set('move');
        overlay.addChild(hover, outline, gizmo, measure, zoom);
        app.stage.addChild(world, overlay);
        app.stage.eventMode = 'static';
        app.stage.hitArea = app.screen;
        app.stage.on('pointerdown', (e) => e.target === app.stage && !e.shiftKey && selection.clear());

        const redlines = () => params.redlines === 'on hover' || altDown();
        const measured = bindMeasure(selection, measure, { between: redlines });
        // while measuring, the hovered layer gets the red outline instead of the blue one
        const syncHover = () => {
            const over = selection.state.hovered.value;
            const quiet = !over || selection.has(over) || (redlines() && selection.primary);

            hover.hover(quiet ? null : over);
        };
        const stops = [
            bindOutline(selection, outline),
            watch(selection.state.hovered, syncHover),
            watch(selection.state.items, syncHover),
            bindGizmo(selection, gizmo),
            measured.stop,
            // every gizmo drag is one undo step, and the keys undo it
            recordGizmo(gizmo, history),
            bindHistoryKeys(history),
        ];

        // an artboard with a few layers on it
        const title = new SilkText({
            text: 'Home',
            fontFamily: 'Inter, system-ui, sans-serif',
            fontSize: 13,
            fill: 0x8e8e93,
        });

        title.position.set(0, -20);
        world.addChild(title);

        const layer = (x: number, y: number, draw: (g: SilkGraphics) => void) => {
            const item = new Container();
            const g = new SilkGraphics();

            draw(g);
            item.addChild(g);
            item.position.set(x, y);
            item.eventMode = 'static';
            item.cursor = 'pointer';
            item.on('pointerover', () => selection.state.hovered.set(item));
            item.on('pointerout', () => {
                if (selection.state.hovered.value === item) selection.state.hovered.set(null);
            });
            item.on('pointerdown', (e) => {
                e.stopPropagation();
                selection.pick(item, e.shiftKey ? 'toggle' : 'replace');
            });
            world.addChild(item);

            return item;
        };

        const board = layer(0, 0, (g) => g.rect(0, 0, 390, 620).fill(0xf4f4f6));

        layer(24, 24, (g) =>
            g.roundRect(0, 0, 342, 180, 24, 0.6).fill(linear([0x5e5ce6, 0xbf5af2], { from: [0, 0], to: [1, 1] })),
        );
        const card = layer(24, 228, (g) =>
            g
                .roundRect(0, 0, 160, 120, 18, 0.6)
                .fill({ color: 0xffffff, innerShadow: { color: 0x000000, alpha: 0.06, y: -1, blur: 1 } }),
        );

        layer(206, 228, (g) => g.roundRect(0, 0, 160, 120, 18, 0.6).fill(0xffffff));
        layer(24, 372, (g) => g.roundRect(0, 0, 342, 64, 16, 0.6).fill(0xffffff));
        layer(48, 388, (g) => g.circle(16, 16, 16).fill(0x30d158));
        layer(24, 532, (g) => g.pill(0, 0, 342, 52).fill(0x1c1c1e));

        const place = () =>
            zoom.position.set(app.screen.width - zoom.size[0] - 12, app.screen.height - zoom.size[1] - 12);

        app.renderer.on('resize', place);
        place();
        selection.pick(card);
        camera.fit(board, 40, false);

        // Alt shows the redlines without moving the pointer
        const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
            if (e.key !== 'Alt') return;
            measured.sync();
            syncHover();
        };

        addEventListener('keydown', onKey);
        addEventListener('keyup', onKey);

        return () => {
            for (const stop of stops) stop();
            removeEventListener('keydown', onKey);
            removeEventListener('keyup', onKey);
            camera.destroy();
        };
    },
});
```

The demo adds redlines and undo to what this page builds. Its source opens in Studio.

## The whole canvas

```ts

// 1. a world the camera moves, and an overlay that stays in screen space
const world = new Container();
const overlay = new Container();
const camera = new Camera({ world, element: app.canvas });
const grid = new CanvasGrid({ camera, ticker: app.ticker });

app.stage.addChild(grid, world, overlay);

// 2. one selection store, with an outline and a gizmo that follow it
const selection = new Selection<Container>();
const outline = new SelectionOutline({ ticker: app.ticker });
const gizmo = new TransformGizmo({ mode: 'move', ticker: app.ticker });

overlay.addChild(outline, gizmo);
bindOutline(selection, outline);
bindGizmo(selection, gizmo);

// 3. layers that select on click
function layer(x: number, y: number, draw: (g: SilkGraphics) => void) {
    const g = new SilkGraphics();

    draw(g);
    g.position.set(x, y);
    g.eventMode = 'static';
    g.cursor = 'pointer';
    g.on('pointerdown', (e) => {
        e.stopPropagation();
        selection.pick(g, e.shiftKey ? 'toggle' : 'replace');
    });
    world.addChild(g);

    return g;
}

const card = layer(0, 0, (g) => g.roundRect(0, 0, 200, 120, 18, 0.6).fill(0xffffff));

layer(240, 20, (g) => g.circle(40, 40, 40).fill(0x30d158));

// 4. a click on empty canvas clears the selection
app.stage.eventMode = 'static';
app.stage.hitArea = app.screen;
app.stage.on('pointerdown', (e) => e.target === app.stage && selection.clear());

selection.pick(card);
camera.fit(world, 40, false);
```

## What each part does

The camera moves and scales `world`. Scroll pans it, and pinch or ctrl + scroll zooms around the
pointer. `camera.fit(world, 40, false)` frames the layers with 40 px of padding and no animation.

The grid sits behind the world and reads the camera, so its lines stay `lineWidth` screen pixels
wide (default 1) at every zoom. Finer levels fade in as you zoom in.

`Selection` is a store with no drawing in it. `bindOutline` and `bindGizmo` subscribe the outline
and the gizmo to it, and each returns a function that stops the binding. Everything that changes
the selection goes through `selection.pick()` or `selection.clear()`.

The outline and the gizmo live in `overlay`, outside the world. They follow their target's
screen position, so the handles keep their size when you zoom. Put overlays inside the world and
they scale with it.

## Options worth changing

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Camera` `wheel` | `'pan'` | `'zoom'` makes the wheel zoom, like a map |
| `Camera` `zoomRange` | `[0.02, 256]` | smallest and largest zoom |
| `Camera` `touchPan` | `'two'` | `'one'` pans with one finger |
| `CanvasGrid` `style` | `'lines'` | `'dots'` draws a dot grid |
| `TransformGizmo` `mode` | `'universal'` | `'move'`, `'rotate'`, `'scale'` or `'box'` shows one kind of handle |

## Where it stops

The kit draws and tracks state. It does not save documents or decide what a layer is. The
selection holds any value you give it, so your own layer objects work as well as containers.

## Where next

- [Canvas & rulers](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/canvas-and-rulers/) adds rulers, guides, a marquee and spacing markers.
- [Gizmos & selection](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/gizmos-and-selection/) covers rotate and scale, snapping and undo.
- [Panels](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/panels/) adds a layer tree and an inspector.

# Shapes

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/shapes/
Section: Shapes & strokes

> Rects and squircles with per-corner radii, circles, ellipses, polygons, stars, arcs, rings and sectors, plus the transform stack that rotates them.

A shape method adds a primitive to the active path, and `fill()` or `stroke()` paints it. Pixi's
`Graphics` works the same way, so `g.rect(...).circle(...).fill(0x0a84ff)` fills both shapes.

Live demo `shapes` (source):

```ts
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// Every shape is centred on (0, 0) and moved into its cell with the transform stack.
const SHAPES: { draw: (g: SilkGraphics) => SilkGraphics; color: number; open?: boolean }[] = [
    { draw: (g) => g.rect(-30, -22, 60, 44), color: 0x0a84ff },
    { draw: (g) => g.roundRect(-30, -22, 60, 44, 14, 0.6), color: 0x5e5ce6 },
    { draw: (g) => g.pill(-34, -14, 68, 28), color: 0xbf5af2 },
    { draw: (g) => g.circle(0, 0, 26), color: 0xff375f },
    { draw: (g) => g.ellipse(0, 0, 34, 20), color: 0xff9f0a },
    { draw: (g) => g.arc(0, 0, 26, -2.5, 0.8), color: 0xffd60a, open: true },
    { draw: (g) => g.sector(0, 0, 30, -2.2, 1.6, 14, 4), color: 0x30d158 },
    { draw: (g) => g.heart(0, 2, 56, 0.12), color: 0xff453a },
    { draw: (g) => g.star(0, 0, 5, 30, undefined, 0, 3), color: 0xffd60a },
    { draw: (g) => g.regularPoly(0, 0, 28, 6, 0, 5), color: 0x64d2ff },
    { draw: (g) => g.triangle(-30, 22, 30, 22, 0, -28, 6), color: 0xac8e68 },
    { draw: (g) => g.polyline([-34, 14, -12, -16, 10, 10, 34, -18]), color: 0xffffff, open: true },
];

export default defineDemo({
    size: [520, 250],
    controls: {
        outline: { type: 'toggle', label: 'outline', value: false },
        spin: { type: 'toggle', label: 'rotate', value: false },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            g.clear();
            SHAPES.forEach((shape, i) => {
                g.save()
                    .translateTransform(50 + (i % 6) * 84, 65 + Math.floor(i / 6) * 120)
                    .rotateTransform(params.spin ? t * 0.6 : 0);
                const path = shape.draw(g);

                if (shape.open) path.stroke({ width: 5, cap: 'round', color: shape.color });
                else if (params.outline) path.stroke({ width: 2, color: shape.color });
                else path.fill(shape.color);
                g.restore();
            });
        });
    },
});
```

```ts
g.roundRect(0, 0, 200, 80, 20, 0.6).fill(0x1c1c1e).stroke({ width: 2, color: 0x3a3a3c });
```

That draws a card with squircle corners and a border. A `stroke()` right after `fill()` lands in
the same primitive, so the two paints meet without a seam. Stroke options are on
[Strokes & dashes](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/strokes-and-dashes/).

## Rectangles, squircles and pills

Live demo `squircle` (source):

```ts
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// A squircle keeps curvature continuous where the side meets the corner (iOS icons, cards).
export default defineDemo({
    size: [420, 220],
    controls: {
        radius: { type: 'range', label: 'radius', min: 0, max: 80, step: 1, value: 48, unit: 'px' },
        smoothing: { type: 'range', label: 'smoothing', min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.01, value: 0.6 },
        compare: { type: 'toggle', label: 'circular overlay', value: true },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick(() => {
            g.clear();
            g.roundRect(110, 20, 200, 180, params.radius, params.smoothing)
                .fill(0x2c2c2e)
                .stroke({ width: 2, color: 0x64d2ff });
            if (params.compare)
                g.roundRect(110, 20, 200, 180, params.radius).stroke({ width: 1, color: 0xff375f, alpha: 0.8 });
        });
    },
});
```

```ts
g.rect(x, y, width, height);
g.roundRect(x, y, width, height, radius);              // circular corners
g.roundRect(x, y, width, height, radius, 0.6);         // squircle corners
g.roundRect(x, y, width, height, [24, 24, 8, 8]);      // per corner: tl, tr, br, bl
g.pill(x, y, width, height);                            // fully round ends
```

The sixth argument, `smoothing`, runs from 0 to 1. Above 0 the corner becomes a superellipse arc
whose curvature grows gradually, the corner of iOS app icons. iOS uses about `0.6`. A smoothed
corner is as deep as a circular one of the same `radius` at its midpoint, so switching keeps the
layout.

## Circles, ellipses and hearts

```ts
g.circle(cx, cy, radius);
g.ellipse(cx, cy, radiusX, radiusY);
g.heart(cx, cy, width, rounding);      // rounding 0 to 0.3 puffs it up
```

## Polygons, stars and triangles

```ts
g.regularPoly(cx, cy, radius, sides, rotation, cornerRadius);   // first vertex points up
g.star(cx, cy, points, radius, innerRadius, rotation, cornerRadius);
g.triangle(x0, y0, x1, y1, x2, y2, cornerRadius);
```

`cornerRadius` rounds every corner with a true circular arc. Leave it at 0 for sharp corners,
which then take the stroke's `join`. For free outlines, use `poly()`, `moveTo()` or `svgPath()` on
[Lines & paths](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/lines-and-paths/).

## Arcs and rings

Live demo `rings` (source):

```ts
import { conic, SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

const RINGS = [
    { r: 78, colors: [0xfa114f, 0xff5e8a] },
    { r: 58, colors: [0x92e82a, 0xd4ff5a] },
    { r: 38, colors: [0x1ee0ff, 0x7df9ff] },
].map((ring) => ({ ...ring, gradient: conic(ring.colors) }));

export default defineDemo({
    size: [260, 200],
    controls: {
        progress: { type: 'range', label: 'progress', min: 0, max: 1.6, step: 0.01, value: 0.8 },
        cap: { type: 'select', label: 'cap', options: ['round', 'butt', 'square'], value: 'round' },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            g.clear();
            RINGS.forEach((ring, i) => {
                const p = Math.max(0.001, params.progress * (1 - i * 0.18) + Math.sin(t + i) * 0.02);

                g.circle(130, 100, ring.r).stroke({ width: 16, color: ring.colors[0], alpha: 0.18 });
                // the conic gradient spans whatever arc it is drawn on
                g.arcSweep(130, 100, ring.r, -Math.PI / 2, Math.PI * 2 * p).stroke({
                    width: 16,
                    cap: params.cap as 'round',
                    gradient: ring.gradient,
                });
            });
        });
    },
});
```

```ts
g.arcSweep(100, 100, 60, -Math.PI / 2, Math.PI * 2 * progress)
    .stroke({ width: 14, cap: 'round', color: 0x30d158 });
```

`arcSweep(cx, cy, radius, startAngle, sweep)` takes a signed sweep that turns clockwise on screen.
`arc(cx, cy, radius, startAngle, endAngle, anticlockwise)` has the Canvas signature. Angles are in
radians with y pointing down, so `-Math.PI / 2` is 12 o'clock. A sweep of a full turn or more
draws a closed ring.

Arcs are open curves, so you stroke them. `cap` defaults to `'butt'`, as in Pixi. Each arc starts a
subpath of its own. Unlike `Graphics.arc`, it does not draw a line from the previous point.

A `conic()` gradient on an arc spans that arc. Its start and sweep default to the arc's own, so the
ramp runs from cap to cap however long the arc is.

```ts
const RING = conic([0xfa114f, 0xff5e8a]);

g.arcSweep(100, 100, 60, -Math.PI / 2, sweep).stroke({ width: 16, cap: 'round', gradient: RING });
```

## Sectors and donut segments

```ts
const slices = [0.4, 0.25, 0.2, 0.15];
const COLORS = [0x0a84ff, 0x30d158, 0xffd60a, 0xff375f];
let a = -Math.PI / 2;

for (const [i, share] of slices.entries()) {
    const sweep = share * Math.PI * 2;

    g.sector(120, 120, 90, a + 0.02, a + sweep - 0.02, 50, 6).fill(COLORS[i]);
    a += sweep;
}
```

`sector(cx, cy, radius, startAngle, endAngle, innerRadius, cornerRadius)` is a closed shape. An
`innerRadius` above 0 turns the pie slice into a donut segment, and `cornerRadius` rounds its four
corners. The loop above draws a donut chart with small gaps between the slices.

## One shape from several

Add `union: true` to paint every shape of the path as one. Overlaps are painted once, so a
translucent arrow made of a shaft and a head shows no darker joint.

```ts
g.rect(0, -2, 40, 4)
    .triangle(36, -8, 50, 0, 36, 8)
    .fill({ color: 0x0a84ff, alpha: 0.6, union: true });
```

Let the shapes overlap a little. A `stroke()` right after a union fill follows the outline of the
union. To cut, intersect or nest shapes, see [Shape operations](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/shape-operations/).

## Rotate and scale with the transform stack

Live demo `transforms` (source):

```ts
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// save / translateTransform / rotateTransform / scaleTransform / restore, like Pixi's GraphicsContext.
export default defineDemo({
    size: [420, 220],
    controls: {
        speed: { type: 'range', label: 'speed', min: 0, max: 3, step: 0.05, value: 1 },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();
        let a = 0;

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((_t, dt) => {
            a += dt * params.speed;
            g.clear();
            g.save().translateTransform(210, 110);
            for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) {
                g.save()
                    .rotateTransform((i / 12) * Math.PI * 2 + a)
                    .translateTransform(70, 0)
                    .scaleTransform(0.6 + 0.4 * Math.sin(a * 2 + i));
                // rotated rects stay exact: rotation is part of the primitive, not a tessellation
                g.roundRect(-14, -8, 28, 16, 8).fill(i % 2 ? 0xff9f0a : 0x5e5ce6);
                g.restore();
            }
            g.star(0, 0, 6, 34, 16, -a, 4).fill(0xffd60a);
            g.restore();
        });
    },
});
```

```ts
g.save()
    .translateTransform(210, 110)
    .rotateTransform(Math.PI / 4)
    .scaleTransform(1.5);
g.roundRect(-20, -10, 40, 20, 8).fill(0xff9f0a);
g.restore();
```

The rect is drawn in the transformed space: moved to (210, 110), turned 45 degrees and scaled by
1.5. `SilkGraphics` has the transform stack of Pixi's `GraphicsContext`.

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `save()`, `restore()` | Push and pop the current transform |
| `translateTransform(x, y = x)` | Move |
| `rotateTransform(angle)` | Rotate, in radians |
| `scaleTransform(x, y = x)` | Scale |
| `setTransform(a, b, c, d, tx, ty)` | Replace the transform with a matrix |
| `resetTransform()` | Go back to the identity |

Shapes are stored already transformed, and rotated rects, ellipses and polygons keep their exact
outline. Stroke widths, dash lengths and blur radii scale with the uniform part of the scale.

The transform stack suits icons and repeated parts that you redraw. For an object that moves as a
whole, such as a card sliding in, give it its own `SilkGraphics` and animate its `position`,
`rotation` or `scale`. That changes one matrix and rebuilds nothing.

---

# Lines & paths

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/lines-and-paths/
Section: Shapes & strokes

> Lines and polylines with monotone or Catmull-Rom smoothing, miter, bevel and round joins, Bezier and SVG paths that fill and stroke, and tapered strokes.

Lines, polylines and paths are the open and free-form shapes of `SilkGraphics`. Stroke them, or
fill a closed path as one shape.

Live demo `polyline` (source):

```ts
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 220],
    controls: {
        width: { type: 'range', label: 'width', min: 0.25, max: 16, step: 0.25, value: 6, unit: 'px' },
        smooth: { type: 'select', label: 'smooth', options: ['none', 'monotone', 'catmull'], value: 'none' },
        alpha: { type: 'range', label: 'alpha', min: 0.1, max: 1, step: 0.05, value: 0.6 },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            const pts: number[] = [];

            for (let i = 0; i <= 12; i++) pts.push(30 + i * 35, 110 + Math.sin(i * 1.3 + t) * 60 * Math.cos(i * 0.7));
            g.clear();
            // translucent on purpose: every pixel is shaded once, so joints never double-blend
            g.polyline(pts, { smooth: params.smooth === 'none' ? undefined : (params.smooth as 'monotone') }).stroke({
                width: params.width,
                color: 0x0a84ff,
                alpha: params.alpha,
                cap: 'round',
            });
            for (let i = 0; i < pts.length; i += 2) g.circle(pts[i], pts[i + 1], 3).fill(0xffffff);
        });
    },
});
```

```ts
g.polyline([20, 140, 80, 40, 140, 110, 200, 30], { smooth: 'catmull' })
    .stroke({ width: 6, color: 0x0a84ff, alpha: 0.6, cap: 'round' });
```

That draws a translucent curve through four points. Every pixel of the stroke is shaded once, so
the corners have the same alpha as the straight parts instead of darker blobs.

## Draw lines and polylines

```ts nocheck
g.line(x0, y0, x1, y1).stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xffffff });
g.polyline(points).stroke(...);
g.polyline(points, { closed: true }).stroke(...);
```

Points can be a flat array `[x0, y0, x1, y1, ...]`, a typed array or an array of `{ x, y }`.

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `closed` | `false` | Connects the last point back to the first |
| `smooth` | `false` | `'monotone'` draws a curve that never overshoots the data, for charts. `'catmull'` draws a free curve through every point. |
| `step` | 2 | Sample spacing of the smoothed curve, in local units |

## Choose a join

Live demo `joins` (source):

```ts
import { type LineJoin, SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 260],
    controls: {
        join: { type: 'select', label: 'join', options: ['miter', 'bevel', 'round'], value: 'miter' },
        width: { type: 'range', label: 'width', min: 1, max: 28, step: 1, value: 16, unit: 'px' },
        miterLimit: { type: 'range', label: 'miter limit', min: 1, max: 10, step: 0.5, value: 4 },
        alpha: { type: 'range', label: 'alpha', min: 0.1, max: 1, step: 0.05, value: 0.6 },
        dash: { type: 'select', label: 'dash', options: ['off', 'on'], value: 'off' },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            const style = {
                width: params.width,
                join: params.join as LineJoin,
                miterLimit: params.miterLimit,
                color: 0x0a84ff,
                alpha: params.alpha,
                dash: params.dash === 'on' ? ([22, 10] as [number, number]) : undefined,
            };
            const zig: number[] = [];

            for (let i = 0; i <= 6; i++) zig.push(30 + i * 30, i % 2 ? 50 : 110 + Math.sin(t) * 10);
            g.clear();
            // translucent on purpose: each path is one distance field, so corners never double-blend
            g.polyline(zig).stroke(style);
            g.rect(260, 40, 80, 70).stroke({ ...style, color: 0x30d158 });
            g.regularPoly(400, 78, 42, 3, t * 0.3).stroke({ ...style, color: 0xff9f0a });
            g.star(90, 190, 5, 52, 22, 0).stroke({ ...style, color: 0xff375f });
            g.moveTo(190, 230)
                .bezierCurveTo(230, 120, 300, 260, 340, 160)
                .lineTo(440, 220)
                .lineTo(380, 150)
                .stroke({ ...style, color: 0xbf5af2, cap: 'round' });
        });
    },
});
```

```ts
g.polyline(points).stroke({ width: 12, join: 'bevel', color: 0x0a84ff, alpha: 0.6 });
g.rect(0, 0, 80, 60).stroke({ width: 8, join: 'miter', miterLimit: 4 });
```

`join` sets how segments meet: `'miter'` (the default, as in Canvas and Pixi), `'bevel'` or
`'round'`. A miter longer than `miterLimit` half widths turns into a bevel. The default limit is 10.

Joins follow Canvas 2D and SVG. A dash that runs through a corner gets the join too. Rects without
a radius, and triangles and polygons without a `cornerRadius`, take the join as well, so a stroked
`rect()` looks like a Canvas one.

## Draw Bezier and SVG paths

```ts
g.moveTo(10, 80)
    .quadraticCurveTo(60, 10, 110, 80)
    .bezierCurveTo(140, 120, 180, 20, 220, 60)
    .lineTo(260, 60)
    .stroke({ width: 3, color: 0xff9f0a, cap: 'round' });
```

The Canvas-style path API has `moveTo`, `lineTo`, `quadraticCurveTo`, `bezierCurveTo` and
`closePath`. Curves are flattened into segments that adapt to the curve.

Paths fill as well as stroke. A fill draws the whole path as one shape, so a bolt, a drop or a
logo outline takes blur, spread and inner shadows like a circle. Overlapping subpaths follow the
even-odd rule: a square inside a square makes a hole.

```ts
g.poly([64, 0, 6, 58, 44, 58, 30, 100, 94, 40, 56, 40]).fill({ color: 0xffd60a, blur: 12 });
g.svgPath('M10 80 Q 60 10 110 80 T 210 80').stroke({ width: 3, color: 0x0a84ff });
```

`poly(points)` adds a closed polygon. `svgPath(d)` reads the `d` attribute of an SVG path. To cut
paths out of other shapes, see [Shape operations](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/shape-operations/).

A fill checks every edge of its path for each pixel. Keep filled paths to a few hundred points.

## Taper a stroke

Live demo `taper` (source):

```ts
import { along, SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

const INK = along([0xff9f0a, 0xff375f, 0xbf5af2]);

export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 220],
    controls: {
        start: { type: 'range', label: 'start width', min: 0, max: 30, step: 0.5, value: 2 },
        end: { type: 'range', label: 'end width', min: 0, max: 30, step: 0.5, value: 22 },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            const pts: number[] = [];

            for (let i = 0; i <= 40; i++) {
                const u = i / 40;

                pts.push(40 + u * 400, 110 + Math.sin(u * 7 + t) * 50 * (1 - u * 0.5));
            }
            g.clear();
            // `width: [start, end]` tapers along the path; an array per point also works
            g.polyline(pts).stroke({ width: [params.start, params.end], cap: 'round', gradient: INK });
        });
    },
});
```

```ts
g.polyline(points).stroke({ width: [2, 22], cap: 'round', gradient: along([0xff9f0a, 0xbf5af2]) });
```

Pass an array as `width`. With two values, the width runs from the first to the second along the
path length. With one value per point, each value sets the width at its vertex. The taper stays
smooth through the joints. `along()` is a gradient that runs from the first point of the stroke to
the last.

## Crossings, fold-backs and dash caps

Live demo `stroke-edges` (source):

```ts
import { type LineJoin, SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// Hard cases of stroked paths, translucent and seen up close. Each pixel is shaded once.
export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 280],
    controls: {
        scene: {
            type: 'select',
            label: 'case',
            options: ['crossing', 'fold-back', 'square dashes'],
            value: 'crossing',
        },
        zoom: { type: 'range', label: 'zoom', min: 1, max: 12, step: 0.5, value: 4, unit: 'x' },
        join: { type: 'select', label: 'join', options: ['miter', 'bevel', 'round'], value: 'miter' },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            g.clear();
            const join = params.join as LineJoin;
            // [x, y] of the spot the zoom centres on
            let focus: [number, number];

            if (params.scene === 'crossing') {
                // 400 segments: the second lobe crosses the first one far along the path
                const pts: number[] = [];

                for (let i = 0; i < 400; i++) {
                    const u = (i / 400) * Math.PI * 2;

                    pts.push(240 + 200 * Math.sin(3 * u + 0.3), 140 + 120 * Math.sin(2 * u));
                }
                g.polyline(pts, { closed: true }).stroke({ width: 14, join, color: 0x0a84ff, alpha: 0.5 });
                focus = [240, 140];
            } else if (params.scene === 'fold-back') {
                // turns of 179 to 180 degrees: the stroke goes back over itself
                const a = ((0.2 + 0.8 * (0.5 + 0.5 * Math.sin(t))) * Math.PI) / 180;

                g.moveTo(80, 140)
                    .lineTo(300, 140)
                    .lineTo(300 - 220 * Math.cos(a), 140 + 220 * Math.sin(a))
                    .stroke({ width: 40, join, miterLimit: 10, color: 0xff9f0a, alpha: 0.6 });
                focus = [300, 140];
            } else {
                // dashes whose square caps overlap their neighbours on a tight curve
                g.moveTo(330, 140);
                for (let k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
                    const a0 = (k * Math.PI) / 2;
                    const a1 = a0 + Math.PI / 2;
                    const c = (4 / 3) * Math.tan(Math.PI / 8) * 90;

                    g.bezierCurveTo(
                        240 + 90 * Math.cos(a0) - c * Math.sin(a0),
                        140 + 90 * Math.sin(a0) + c * Math.cos(a0),
                        240 + 90 * Math.cos(a1) + c * Math.sin(a1),
                        140 + 90 * Math.sin(a1) - c * Math.cos(a1),
                        240 + 90 * Math.cos(a1),
                        140 + 90 * Math.sin(a1),
                    );
                }
                g.stroke({ width: 22, join, cap: 'square', dash: [6, 5], color: 0x30d158, alpha: 0.5 });
                focus = [330, 140];
            }
            g.scale.set(params.zoom);
            g.position.set(240 - focus[0] * params.zoom, 140 - focus[1] * params.zoom);
        });

        return undefined;
    },
});
```

A translucent stroke stays one shape in the hard cases too.

A path that crosses itself far along its length is shaded once where it overlaps. A path that
turns back by 180 degrees, or nearly, goes back over itself with no doubled pixels. A full reversal
has no join, as in Canvas. On a curve, square dash caps that overlap the next dash merge into it.

The limit is lines thinner than a pixel. There, crossings of far-apart parts of one path can blend
twice.

## Long paths

A path stroke checks the segments of its path for each pixel. Subpaths longer than 32 segments are
split into chunks, so a long chart line stays fast. Each chunk also checks the segments of other
chunks that come near it, which keeps crossings shaded once. A tapered stroke keeps one capsule
per segment.

---

# Strokes & dashes

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/strokes-and-dashes/
Section: Shapes & strokes

> Paint styles for fill() and stroke(), inside or outside stroke alignment, hairlines that fade instead of breaking up, and dashes and dots with caps.

`fill()` and `stroke()` take a colour, a gradient or a style object. This page covers the stroke
side: width, alignment, hairlines and dashes.

Live demo `dashes` (source):

```ts
import { SilkGraphics, type StrokeStyle } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 220],
    controls: {
        dash: { type: 'range', label: 'dash', min: 0, max: 30, step: 1, value: 10 },
        gap: { type: 'range', label: 'gap', min: 2, max: 30, step: 1, value: 8 },
        cap: { type: 'select', label: 'cap', options: ['butt', 'round', 'square'], value: 'round' },
        march: { type: 'toggle', label: 'animate', value: true },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            const style: StrokeStyle = {
                width: 6,
                cap: params.cap as StrokeStyle['cap'],
                dash: [params.dash, params.gap],
                dashOffset: params.march ? t * 24 : 0,
            };

            g.clear();
            g.circle(90, 110, 70).stroke({ ...style, color: 0x64d2ff }); // on closed outlines the pattern tiles without a seam
            g.line(200, 40, 440, 40).stroke({ ...style, color: 0xffd60a });
            g.polyline([200, 180, 260, 90, 320, 160, 380, 80, 440, 150], { smooth: 'catmull' }).stroke({
                ...style,
                color: 0xff375f,
            });
            g.line(200, 110, 440, 110).stroke({ width: 8, cap: 'round', dash: [0, 16], color: 0x30d158 }); // 0-length dashes = dots
        });
    },
});
```

```ts
g.circle(90, 90, 60).stroke({ width: 4, color: 0x64d2ff, dash: [10, 6] });
```

That draws a dashed ring: 10 units of dash, 6 of gap. The pattern is computed in the shader along
the path length, and every dash gets its own caps.

## Paint styles

```ts
g.circle(0, 0, 20).fill(0xff375f);                                   // any Pixi ColorSource
g.circle(0, 0, 20).fill('rgba(255, 55, 95, 0.5)');
g.circle(0, 0, 20).fill(linear([0x0a84ff, 0xbf5af2]));               // a gradient
g.circle(0, 0, 20).fill({ color: 0xff375f, alpha: 0.5, blur: 6 });   // a FillStyle
g.circle(0, 0, 20).stroke({ width: 4, color: 0xffffff, alignment: 'inside' });
```

`FillStyle` holds `color`, `alpha`, `gradient` and the effects on
[Shadows & effects](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/shadows-and-effects/). With a gradient, `color` tints it.
`StrokeStyle` adds these:

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | 1 | Stroke width in local units. An array tapers it ([Lines & paths](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/lines-and-paths/#taper-a-stroke)). |
| `alignment` | `'center'` | `'inside'`, `'center'` or `'outside'` the edge, or Pixi's numbers (1, 0.5, 0) |
| `cap` | `'butt'` | Ends of open paths and of every dash: `'butt'`, `'round'` or `'square'` |
| `join` | `'miter'` | Corners: `'miter'`, `'bevel'` or `'round'` |
| `miterLimit` | 10 | A longer miter, in half widths, becomes a bevel |
| `dash` | none | `[dash, gap]`, or one number for equal dash and gap |
| `dashOffset` | 0 | Shifts the pattern along the path, in local units |
| `dashFit` | `true` | Stretches the pattern on closed outlines so it tiles without a short dash |

## Align a stroke inside or outside

Live demo `alignment` (source):

```ts
import { Text } from 'pixi.js';
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

const MODES = ['inside', 'center', 'outside'] as const;

export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 200],
    controls: {
        width: { type: 'range', label: 'stroke width', min: 1, max: 24, step: 1, value: 12, unit: 'px' },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();

        stage.addChild(g);
        MODES.forEach((mode, i) => {
            const label = new Text({ text: mode, style: { fill: 0x8e8e93, fontSize: 13, fontFamily: 'system-ui' } });

            label.anchor.set(0.5, 0);
            label.position.set(90 + i * 150, 168);
            stage.addChild(label);
        });
        tick(() => {
            g.clear();
            MODES.forEach((alignment, i) => {
                const x = 40 + i * 150;

                // fill + stroke on the same shape share one instance and never leave a seam
                g.roundRect(x, 40, 100, 100, 22, 0.6)
                    .fill(0x2c2c2e)
                    .stroke({ width: params.width, color: 0x30d158, alpha: 0.85, alignment });
                g.roundRect(x, 40, 100, 100, 22, 0.6).stroke({ width: 1, color: 0xffffff, alpha: 0.6 }); // the geometric edge
            });
        });
    },
});
```

Strokes on closed shapes sit inside the edge, centred on it or outside it. Strokes on open shapes,
such as lines and arcs, are always centred.

When `stroke()` follows `fill()` directly, both paints go into one primitive. The shader splits
each pixel's coverage between the fill and the stroke band. An inside stroke drawn this way has no
halo of fill colour along its outer edge, which a stroke drawn on top of a separate fill shows.

## Hairlines

Live demo `hairlines` (source):

```ts
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// Lines thinner than a device pixel keep one pixel of width and fade instead of breaking up.
export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 220],
    controls: {
        scale: { type: 'range', label: 'width scale', min: 0.05, max: 2, step: 0.01, value: 0.5 },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            g.clear();
            for (let i = 0; i < 24; i++) {
                const a = -Math.PI / 2 + (i / 23) * Math.PI + Math.sin(t * 0.3) * 0.05;
                const w = (0.1 + i * 0.12) * params.scale;

                g.line(240, 200, 240 + Math.cos(a) * 220, 200 + Math.sin(a) * 190).stroke({
                    width: w,
                    color: 0xffffff,
                });
            }
        });
    },
});
```

A screen cannot show a stroke thinner than one device pixel. Silk keeps such a stroke one pixel
wide and scales its alpha by its width. A 0.25 px line is drawn 1 px wide at 25% alpha, so the ink
stays in proportion. Lines never break into dots, and a zoomed-out drawing keeps every line.

The threshold is `minStrokePx`, a per-object setting:

```ts
const lines = new SilkGraphics({ minStrokePx: 1, aaWidth: 1, dither: 1 });

lines.aaWidth = 1.5;   // softer edges
```

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `minStrokePx` | 1 | Strokes thinner than this many device pixels keep this width and fade |
| `aaWidth` | 1 | Width of the anti-aliasing ramp, in device pixels |
| `dither` | 1 | Dither of gradients and blurs, in 8-bit steps. 0 turns it off |

`SilkGraphics.defaults` holds the defaults for new objects.

## Dots

```ts
g.line(0, 20, 300, 20).stroke({ width: 8, cap: 'round', dash: [0, 16], color: 0x30d158 });
```

A dash of length 0 draws a dot with `cap: 'round'` and a square with `cap: 'square'`. The pattern
repeats every `dash + gap` units, so `[0, 16]` places a dot every 16 units.

## Marching ants

```ts
app.ticker.add(() => {
    g.clear().circle(80, 80, 56).stroke({ width: 3, color: 0xffffff, dash: [6, 6], dashOffset: t * 30 });
});
```

Animate `dashOffset` to move the pattern along the path. A selection outline or a loading
spinner is a dashed stroke with a growing offset.

## Where dashes work

Dashes work on lines, polylines, paths, arcs, circles and ellipses. Sharp rects, triangles and
polygons dash too with a miter or bevel join, because their strokes then run as paths. Rounded rects, rounded polygons, sectors
and hearts draw a solid stroke. For a dashed card border, stroke a path through the corners, or
`svgPath()` with arcs.

On closed outlines, `dashFit` stretches the pattern a little so it tiles the perimeter. Without
it, a short dash appears where the outline starts. Set `dashFit: false` to keep the exact lengths.

---

# Shape operations

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/shape-operations/
Section: Shapes & strokes

> Union, subtract, intersect and exclude shapes and SVG paths in PixiJS with fill({ op }) and boolean(). Results take strokes, gradients, blur and hit tests.

Shape operations combine several shapes into one: cut a hole in a card, make a ring from two
circles or build an icon from a few primitives.

Live demo `shape-ops` (source):

```ts
import { conic, type ShapeOp, SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// Shape operations: one exact shape from many. Each result is one instance, painted once.
export default defineDemo({
    size: [520, 280],
    controls: {
        op: {
            type: 'select',
            label: 'op',
            options: ['union', 'subtract', 'intersect', 'exclude'],
            value: 'subtract',
        },
        stroke: { type: 'toggle', label: 'stroke', value: true },
        blur: { type: 'range', label: 'blur', min: 0, max: 12, step: 1, value: 0, unit: 'px' },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();
        const ringPaint = conic([0x30d158, 0xffd60a, 0x30d158]);

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            const op = params.op as ShapeOp;
            const outline = params.stroke ? { width: 3, color: 0xffffff, alpha: 0.9 } : null;
            const dx = Math.sin(t * 0.8) * 14;

            g.clear();
            // two circles combined by the picked op, translucent so double painting would show
            g.circle(76, 110, 52)
                .circle(124 + dx, 110, 52)
                .fill({ color: 0x0a84ff, alpha: 0.75, op, blur: params.blur });
            if (outline) g.stroke({ ...outline, op });

            // a ring with a notch: a circle minus a smaller circle and a bar
            g.boolean(
                'subtract',
                (g) => g.circle(250, 110, 56),
                (g) => g.circle(250, 110, 34).rect(244, 40, 12, 40),
            ).fill({ gradient: ringPaint, blur: params.blur });
            if (outline) g.stroke(outline);

            // an icon: a rounded card minus a cutout keyhole, plus a dot
            g.boolean(
                'union',
                (g) =>
                    g.boolean(
                        'subtract',
                        (g) => g.roundRect(340, 54, 112, 112, 30, 0.6),
                        (g) => g.circle(396, 98, 20).triangle(386, 104, 406, 104, 396, 140, 3),
                    ),
                (g) => g.circle(452, 54, 14),
            ).fill({
                color: 0xff375f,
                blur: params.blur,
                innerShadow: { y: 3, blur: 4, color: 0xffffff, alpha: 0.5 },
            });
            if (outline) g.stroke(outline);

            // an SVG path, a star cut out of it
            g.svgPath('M60 250 C 60 200 140 200 140 250 C 140 280 60 280 60 250 Z')
                .star(100, 240, 5, 18, 8)
                .fill({ color: 0xbf5af2, op: 'subtract', blur: params.blur });
            g.svgPath('M180 270 l30 -60 l30 60 z m30 -42 l-12 30 h24 z').fill({ color: 0xff9f0a, blur: params.blur });
            if (outline) g.stroke(outline);
        });

        return undefined;
    },
});
```

```ts
g.circle(60, 60, 50).circle(60, 60, 30).fill({ color: 0x30d158, op: 'subtract' });
```

That draws a ring: the first circle minus the second. The result is painted once, so a
translucent fill has no darker overlaps.

## Combine the shapes of a path

Add `op` to `fill()` or `stroke()`. It combines every closed shape on the active path.

```ts
g.rect(0, 0, 80, 80).circle(80, 80, 40).fill({ color: 0x0a84ff, op: 'intersect' }); // a quarter disc
g.circle(40, 40, 30).circle(70, 40, 30).fill({ color: 0xff375f, op: 'exclude' });   // two lenses
```

| `op` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `'union'` | Everything any shape covers. The same as `union: true`. |
| `'subtract'` | The first shape minus every later one |
| `'intersect'` | Only what every shape covers |
| `'exclude'` | What an odd number of shapes cover |

A `stroke()` right after the fill follows the outline of the result. A stroke with its own `op`
strokes the outline without a fill.

```ts
g.roundRect(0, 0, 120, 80, 16)
    .circle(60, 40, 24)
    .fill({ color: 0x1c1c1e, op: 'subtract' })
    .stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xffffff });
```

Open shapes take no part. Arcs and areas in the path stroke on their own.

## Nest operations with boolean()

`boolean(op, a, b)` adds one shape to the active path: what callback `a` draws, combined by `op`
with what callback `b` draws. The shapes inside each callback are merged first. A callback can call
`boolean()` again, so any tree of operations works.

```ts
// a ring with a notch, and a dot in the middle
g.boolean(
    'union',
    (g) =>
        g.boolean(
            'subtract',
            (g) => g.circle(50, 50, 40),
            (g) => g.circle(50, 50, 24).rect(46, 0, 8, 30),
        ),
    (g) => g.circle(50, 50, 8),
).fill(0xff9f0a);
```

The callbacks only add shapes. Do not call `fill()` or `stroke()` inside them. Up to 8 operands
can wait on each other at once. A deeper tree is skipped with a warning.

## Cut with SVG paths

```ts
g.svgPath('M12 2 L22 22 H2 Z').fill(0xffd60a);
g.svgPath('M4 4 H20 V20 H4 Z').circle(12, 12, 4).fill({ color: 0xffffff, op: 'subtract' });
```

`svgPath(d)` reads the `d` attribute of an SVG path into the active path. It supports `M`, `L`,
`H`, `V`, `C`, `S`, `Q`, `T`, `A` and `Z`, absolute and relative. A fill draws it as one even-odd
shape, so the inner square of `M0 0 H60 V60 H0 Z M20 20 V40 H40 V20 Z` is a hole.

In a shape operation, a path from `svgPath()` or `moveTo()` is one operand with all its subpaths.
With `'union'`, each subpath counts on its own.

## Paint, effects and hit tests

Everything that paints a closed shape works on the result: colours, gradients, `blur`, a
progressive blur, `spread`, inner shadows and `blend: 'add'`. Gradients in shape units span the
bounds of the result.

The outline of the result is exact. Inside the shape and far outside it, the combined distance is
a close bound instead. A blur, spread or inner shadow wider than a corner can round that corner a
little more than on a plain shape. Keep blurs in proportion for crisp cutouts.

`containsPoint()` follows the result. A ring is hollow, a cutout lets clicks through and an
intersection only hits where the shapes overlap.

## Cost

A combined shape is one instance. Each pixel evaluates every shape in it once, so ten shapes in an
operation cost about what ten separate shapes cost. A path in an operation costs one step per edge.

---

# Gradients

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/gradients/
Section: Paint

> Linear, radial, conic, mesh and along-the-path gradients in OKLab with smooth easing, and half-float ramps with dither that stop dark gradients banding.

A gradient goes anywhere a colour goes: `fill(gradient)`, `stroke({ gradient })`, or
`fill({ gradient, color })`, where `color` tints the ramp.

Live demo `gradients` (source):

```ts
import { Text } from 'pixi.js';
import { conic, linear, radial, SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 240],
    controls: {
        space: { type: 'select', label: 'space', options: ['oklab', 'linear', 'srgb'], value: 'oklab' },
        easing: { type: 'select', label: 'easing', options: ['linear', 'smooth'], value: 'linear' },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();
        const label = new Text({ text: '', style: { fill: 0x8e8e93, fontSize: 12, fontFamily: 'system-ui' } });

        label.position.set(20, 214);
        stage.addChild(g, label);
        tick(() => {
            const options = { space: params.space as 'oklab', easing: params.easing as 'linear' };

            g.clear();
            // gradient objects are cheap: ramps with the same stops share one atlas row
            g.roundRect(20, 20, 440, 50, 14).fill(linear([0x0a84ff, 0xffd60a], options));
            g.roundRect(20, 84, 440, 50, 14).fill(linear([0xff375f, 0x30d158, 0x5e5ce6], options));
            g.circle(80, 180, 26).fill(radial([0xffffff, 0xff9f0a, [1, 0xff375f, 0]], options));
            g.circle(160, 180, 26).fill(conic([0xff375f, 0xffd60a, 0x30d158, 0x64d2ff, 0xbf5af2, 0xff375f], options));
            g.arcSweep(240, 180, 22, 0, Math.PI * 1.6).stroke({
                width: 10,
                cap: 'round',
                gradient: conic([0x30d158, 0xff453a], options),
            });
            label.text = `interpolated in ${params.space}, ${params.easing} easing`;
        });
    },
});
```

```ts
const SUNSET = linear([0xff375f, 0xffd60a, 0x0a84ff], { from: [0, 0], to: [1, 1], easing: 'smooth' });

g.roundRect(0, 0, 240, 120, 24, 0.6).fill(SUNSET);
```

That fills a card with a diagonal three-colour ramp. Build a gradient once and reuse it: each new
gradient object bakes a new ramp.

## Pick a kind

```ts
linear(stops, { from: [0, 0], to: [1, 1] });       // diagonal across the shape's box
vertical(stops);                                    // top to bottom of the shape
horizontal(stops);                                  // left to right
radial(stops, { center: [0.3, 0.3], radius: 0.8, innerRadius: 0.2 });
conic(stops, { startAngle, sweep });                // around a centre
along(stops);                                       // along a stroke, first point to last
```

On an arc or a sector, `conic()` spans the arc by default, so a ring's ramp runs from cap to cap.
`along()` works on strokes of lines, polylines and paths.

## Write the stops

```ts
linear([0xff375f, 0x0a84ff]);                           // spread evenly
linear([[0, 0xff375f], [0.3, 0xffd60a], [1, 0x0a84ff]]);
linear([[0, 0xffffff, 1], [1, 0xffffff, 0]]);            // [offset, color, alpha]
linear([{ offset: 0.5, color: '#30d158', alpha: 0.5 }]);
linear([[0, RED], [0.5, RED], [0.5, BLUE], [1, BLUE]]);  // a hard stop
```

Offsets are clamped to 0 to 1 and made non-decreasing, as in CSS.

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `space` | `'oklab'` | Interpolation space: `'oklab'`, `'linear'` or `'srgb'` |
| `easing` | `'linear'` | `'smooth'` runs a monotone spline through the stops. A function `(t) => number` remaps the ramp. |
| `extend` | `'pad'` | Outside 0 to 1: hold the end colours (`'pad'`), tile (`'repeat'`) or mirror (`'reflect'`) |
| `units` | `'shape'` | `'shape'` measures points in fractions of each shape's box. `'local'` uses the graphics' local units. |

OKLab is a perceptual space. A red-to-green ramp passes through yellow instead of a muddy brown,
and lightness changes evenly. Use `'linear'` for light falloff and `'srgb'` to match CSS.
Interpolation is premultiplied, so a colour fading to transparent never darkens.

`easing: 'smooth'` removes the bright and dark lines the eye sees at each stop of a linear ramp. It
never overshoots the stop colours.

With `units: 'shape'`, one gradient fits every shape it paints. With `units: 'local'`, one ramp
spans many shapes, such as the bars of a chart or a row of pills.

## Mesh gradients

Live demo `effects-mesh` (source):

```ts
import { Container } from 'pixi.js';
import { linear, mesh, SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// A light beam over a lit tablet. A linear gradient can only fade upwards, so its sides stay hard.
// A 3 x 3 mesh also fades towards the sides. Drag a yellow handle up or down to change its brightness.
const LIGHT = 0xffd9ec;
const BOX = { x0: 150, y0: 40, x1: 450, y1: 262 };

export default defineDemo({
    size: [600, 340],
    background: 0x2e2f7a,
    touchAction: 'none',
    controls: {
        paint: { type: 'select', label: 'beam', options: ['mesh', 'linear'], value: 'mesh' },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const beam = new SilkGraphics();
        const tablet = new SilkGraphics();
        const handles = new SilkGraphics();
        const hit = new Container();
        // brightness of the control points, top row first
        const alpha = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0.35, 0, 0.15, 1, 0.15];
        let grab: { i: number; y: number; a: number } | null = null;
        let drawn = '';

        const point = (i: number) => ({
            x: BOX.x0 + ((i % 3) / 2) * (BOX.x1 - BOX.x0),
            y: BOX.y0 + (Math.floor(i / 3) / 2) * (BOX.y1 - BOX.y0),
        });

        tablet.triangle(165, 262, 435, 262, 470, 300, 2).fill(0x1d1e52);
        tablet.triangle(165, 262, 130, 300, 470, 300, 2).fill(0x1d1e52);
        tablet.roundRect(170, 266, 260, 26, 4).fill(0xffe2ee);
        tablet.rect(130, 300, 340, 9).fill(0x15163d);

        hit.eventMode = 'static';
        hit.hitArea = { contains: () => true };
        hit.on('pointerdown', (e) => {
            if (params.paint !== 'mesh') return;
            const p = e.getLocalPosition(stage);
            const i = alpha.findIndex((_, k) => Math.hypot(point(k).x - p.x, point(k).y - p.y) < 20);

            grab = i < 0 ? null : { i, y: p.y, a: alpha[i] };
        });
        hit.on('globalpointermove', (e) => {
            if (!grab) return;
            alpha[grab.i] = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, grab.a - (e.getLocalPosition(stage).y - grab.y) / 120));
        });
        hit.on('pointerup', () => (grab = null));
        hit.on('pointerupoutside', () => (grab = null));
        stage.addChild(beam, tablet, handles, hit);

        tick(() => {
            const key = `${params.paint}|${alpha.join(',')}`;

            if (key === drawn) return;
            drawn = key;
            const units = { units: 'local' as const };
            const paint =
                params.paint === 'mesh'
                    ? mesh(
                          3,
                          3,
                          alpha.map((a) => [LIGHT, a] as [number, number]),
                          { ...units, from: [BOX.x0, BOX.y0], to: [BOX.x1, BOX.y1] },
                      )
                    : linear(
                          [
                              [0, LIGHT, 0],
                              [1, LIGHT, 1],
                          ],
                          { ...units, from: [0, BOX.y0], to: [0, BOX.y1] },
                      );

            beam.clear();
            beam.rect(BOX.x0, BOX.y0, BOX.x1 - BOX.x0, BOX.y1 - BOX.y0).fill(paint);

            handles.clear();
            if (params.paint !== 'mesh') return;
            handles.rect(BOX.x0, BOX.y0, BOX.x1 - BOX.x0, BOX.y1 - BOX.y0).stroke({
                width: 1,
                color: 0xffef6e,
                alpha: 0.4,
                dash: [4, 4],
            });
            alpha.forEach((a, i) => {
                const p = point(i);

                handles
                    .circle(p.x, p.y, 6)
                    .fill({ color: 0xffef6e, alpha: 0.2 + a * 0.8 })
                    .stroke({ width: 1.5, color: 0xffef6e });
            });
        });

        return undefined;
    },
});
```

```ts

const beam = mesh(3, 3, [
    [0xffd9ec, 0], [0xffd9ec, 0], [0xffd9ec, 0],
    [0xffd9ec, 0.1], [0xffd9ec, 0.4], [0xffd9ec, 0.1],
    [0xffd9ec, 0.5], [0xffd9ec, 1], [0xffd9ec, 0.5],
]);
g.rect(0, 0, 380, 220).fill(beam);
```

`mesh(cols, rows, colors)` takes a grid of control colours, row by row from the top left. Each is
a colour or `[color, alpha]`. The grid blends into one smooth surface in OKLab that passes through
every control colour. A grid has at most 16 by 16 colours.

The beam above fades towards the top and towards both sides, which no linear gradient can do. Pass
`from` and `to` with `units: 'local'` to share one mesh across several shapes.

## Banding

Live demo `dither` (source):

```ts
import { ColorMatrixFilter, Container } from 'pixi.js';
import { SilkGraphics, vertical } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// A dark, wide gradient has only a few 8-bit steps. Half-float ramps + ±½ LSB dither hide them.
const NIGHT = vertical([0x0b1026, 0x1d1a3a, 0x10141f]);

export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 220],
    background: 0x000000,
    controls: {
        dither: { type: 'toggle', label: 'dither', value: true },
        reveal: { type: 'toggle', label: 'reveal x8', value: true },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const view = new Container();
        const g = new SilkGraphics();
        // multiply the contrast by 8 around black so every banding step shows
        const reveal = new ColorMatrixFilter();

        reveal.brightness(8, false);
        view.addChild(g);
        stage.addChild(view);
        g.rect(0, 0, 480, 220).fill(NIGHT);
        g.circle(360, 70, 60).fill({ color: 0xffd9a0, alpha: 0.12, blur: 40 });
        tick(() => {
            g.dither = params.dither ? 1 : 0;
            view.filters = params.reveal ? [reveal] : [];
        });
    },
});
```

A dark, wide gradient has only a few 8-bit steps to cover a lot of pixels, so you see bands. Silk
bakes each ramp into a shared 256-wide half-float atlas and adds about half a step of noise per
pixel when it samples. The noise breaks the bands up below what the eye picks out.

Dither applies to gradients and blurs, never to flat colours. Its strength is the per-object
`dither` setting, in 8-bit steps: 1 by default, 0 to turn it off. Turn it off when you read pixels
back and need exact values.

---

# Shadows & effects

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/shadows-and-effects/
Section: Paint

> Blur a fill or stroke into glows and soft shadows, grow it with spread, add Figma-style inner shadows, progressive blur and plus-lighter blends, without filters.

Every paint takes a `blur`. A blurred copy under a crisp shape is a glow or a soft shadow, drawn
like any other shape, without a filter or a render texture.

Live demo `glow` (source):
