# Charts

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/charts/
Section: Examples

> Build area and line charts with monotone smoothing that never overshoots, fading gradient fills, dashed guides, bars and dots in SilkGraphics.

pixi-silk has no chart component. It gives you the pieces a chart is drawn with: filled areas,
smoothed series, dashed guides and bars. The experiments at the end of this page are complete chart
widgets built from them.

Live demo `area-chart` (source):

```ts
import { SilkGraphics, vertical } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

const FILL = vertical(
    [
        [0, 0x0a84ff, 0.55],
        [1, 0x0a84ff, 0],
    ],
    { easing: 'smooth' },
);

export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 220],
    controls: {
        smooth: { type: 'toggle', label: 'monotone smoothing', value: true },
        dots: { type: 'toggle', label: 'dots', value: true },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();
        const data = Array.from({ length: 13 }, (_, i) => 90 + Math.sin(i * 0.9) * 40);

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            const pts = data.flatMap((v, i) => [30 + i * 35, v + Math.sin(t * 1.5 + i) * 12]);
            const smooth = params.smooth ? ('monotone' as const) : undefined;

            g.clear();
            for (const y of [40, 90, 140]) g.line(20, y, 460, y).stroke({ width: 1, color: 0x3a3a3c, dash: [2, 4] });
            g.line(20, 190, 460, 190).stroke({ width: 1, color: 0x636366 });
            // area between the series and a baseline; stroke() right after draws its top line
            g.area(pts, 190, { smooth }).fill(FILL).stroke({ width: 2.5, color: 0x0a84ff, cap: 'round' });
            if (params.dots)
                for (let i = 0; i < pts.length; i += 2)
                    g.circle(pts[i], pts[i + 1], 3.5)
                        .fill(0xffffff)
                        .stroke({ width: 2, color: 0x0a84ff });
        });
    },
});
```

## Fill the area under a series

```ts
const FILL = vertical(
    [
        [0, 0x0a84ff, 0.55],
        [1, 0x0a84ff, 0],
    ],
    { easing: 'smooth' },
);

g.area(points, 190, { smooth: 'monotone' }).fill(FILL).stroke({ width: 2.5, color: 0x0a84ff, cap: 'round' });
```

`area(points, lower)` fills the region between a series and a y baseline. Pass a second series as
`lower` to fill the band between two series. The `stroke()` right after it draws the series line on
top, from the same smoothed points.

The area is split into vertical columns that share their edges exactly. A translucent fill stays
even, with no seams between columns.

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `smooth` | `false` | `'monotone'` draws a smooth curve through the points |
| `step` | `2` | Sample spacing of the smoothed curve, in local units |

## Smoothing that keeps the data

`smooth: 'monotone'` never overshoots. It uses Steffen's method, like d3's `curveMonotoneX`. Peaks
stay on the data points and flat runs stay flat. `polyline()` also takes `smooth: 'catmull'`, which
overshoots, so keep it for decorative curves. `monotoneX()` returns the resampled points if you need
them for hit testing or labels.

## Guides, bars and dots

```ts
for (const y of [40, 90, 140]) g.line(20, y, 460, y).stroke({ width: 1, color: 0x3a3a3c, dash: [2, 4] });
for (const [i, v] of values.entries()) g.roundRect(20 + i * 12, 190 - v, 8, v, 3).fill(0xffd60a);
for (const [x, y] of points) g.circle(x, y, 3.5).fill(0xffffff).stroke({ width: 2, color: 0x0a84ff });
```

Guides are dashed lines, bars are rounded rects and dots are circles with a stroke. All of them go
into the same `SilkGraphics` as the series.

## One gradient across many bars

By default a gradient fits each shape's box. With `units: 'local'` it uses the coordinates of the
graphics instead, so a row of bars samples one continuous ramp:

```ts
const HEAT = linear(
    [
        [0, 0x30d158],
        [0.5, 0xffd60a],
        [1, 0xff453a],
    ],
    { units: 'local', from: [0, 190], to: [0, 40] },
);

for (const [i, v] of values.entries()) g.roundRect(20 + i * 12, 190 - v, 8, v, 3).fill(HEAT);
```

A tall bar then reaches the red end and a short one stays green. [Gradients](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/gradients/)
covers the other gradient kinds and options.

## Where it stops

There are no axes, scales, tick generation or tooltips. Map your data to pixels yourself, or with a
scale library such as d3-scale, and draw labels with [text](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/text/).

---

# Renderers

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/renderers/
Section: Reference

> pixi-silk renders on WebGL2 by default and on WebGPU when you ask for it. How to pick one, set up your own Pixi app and turn on batching.

pixi-silk renders on WebGL2 by default and on WebGPU when you ask for it. Both run the same
shader, a GLSL program and its WGSL port, so a scene looks the same on either.

Live demo `webgpu` (source):

```ts
import { along, conic, linear, mesh, radial, SilkGraphics, vertical } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// The same scene on both renderers: WebGL2 runs the GLSL shader, WebGPU its WGSL port.
// Each cell uses a different part of the shader: every shape, dashes, caps, alignment,
// hairlines, blur, spread, progressive blur, inner shadows, every gradient kind and plus-lighter.
const CELL = 72;

export default defineDemo({
    size: [440, 300],
    renderers: ['webgl', 'webgpu'],
    controls: {
        spin: { type: 'toggle', label: 'rotate', value: false },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();

        stage.addChild(g);
        tick((t) => {
            const a = params.spin ? t * 0.5 : 0;
            const cells: ((g: SilkGraphics) => void)[] = [
                (g) => g.roundRect(-28, -22, 56, 44, 14, 0.6).fill(linear([0x0a84ff, 0xbf5af2])),
                (g) => g.circle(0, 0, 26).fill(radial([0xffffff, 0xff9f0a, [1, 0xff375f, 0]])),
                (g) => g.ellipse(0, 0, 30, 20).stroke({ width: 4, color: 0x64d2ff, dash: [0, 9], cap: 'round' }),
                (g) =>
                    g.arcSweep(0, 0, 22, -Math.PI / 2, Math.PI * 1.5).stroke({
                        width: 9,
                        cap: 'round',
                        gradient: conic([0x30d158, 0xffd60a, 0xff453a]),
                    }),
                (g) => g.sector(0, 0, 28, -2.2, 1.4, 12, 4).fill(0x30d158),
                (g) => g.heart(0, 2, 54, 0.12).fill({ color: 0xff375f, blur: 6, blend: 'add' }),
                (g) =>
                    g
                        .star(0, 0, 5, 28, undefined, 0, 3)
                        .fill(0xffd60a)
                        .stroke({ width: 3, color: 0xffffff, alignment: 'outside' }),
                (g) =>
                    g.triangle(-26, 20, 26, 20, 0, -26, 5).stroke({ width: 4, color: 0xac8e68, alignment: 'inside' }),
                (g) =>
                    g
                        .beginPath()
                        .moveTo(-26, 18)
                        .bezierCurveTo(-30, -30, 10, -10, 4, -2)
                        .bezierCurveTo(30, -30, 30, 20, -26, 18)
                        .closePath()
                        .fill(vertical([0xff9f0a, 0xff375f])),
                (g) =>
                    g.polyline([-30, 16, -12, -14, 8, 10, 30, -18], { smooth: 'catmull' }).stroke({
                        width: [2, 9],
                        cap: 'round',
                        gradient: along([0x5e5ce6, 0x64d2ff]),
                    }),
                (g) =>
                    g.area([-30, 10, -15, -6, 0, 2, 15, -16, 30, -8], 20, { smooth: 'monotone' }).fill(
                        vertical([
                            [0, 0x30d158, 0.9],
                            [1, 0x30d158, 0.05],
                        ]),
                    ),
                (g) => {
                    for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++)
                        g.line(-28, -18 + i * 7, 28, -18 + i * 7).stroke({ width: 0.25 + i * 0.25, color: 0xffffff });
                },
                (g) =>
                    g
                        .roundRect(-22, -16, 44, 32, 8)
                        .fill({ color: 0x0a84ff, alpha: 0.9, blur: 7, spread: 4 })
                        .roundRect(-22, -16, 44, 32, 8)
                        .fill(0x1c1c1e),
                (g) =>
                    g.roundRect(-26, -22, 52, 44, 12).fill({
                        color: 0x1c1c1e,
                        innerShadow: [
                            { color: 0x6694ff, x: 0, y: -10, blur: 8, spread: -2 },
                            { color: 0xffffff, alpha: 0.5, x: 0, y: 4, blur: 2, blend: 'add' },
                        ],
                    }),
                (g) => g.roundRect(-26, -22, 52, 44, 10).fill({ color: 0xff9f0a, blur: { from: 0, to: 9 } }),
                (g) => g.roundRect(-28, -22, 56, 44, 6).fill(mesh(2, 2, [0xff375f, 0x0a84ff, 0xffd60a, 0x30d158])),
                (g) => g.circle(0, 0, 24).stroke({ width: 6, color: 0xbf5af2, dash: [10, 6], cap: 'butt' }),
                (g) => g.regularPoly(0, 0, 26, 6, 0, 5).fill({ gradient: linear([0x64d2ff, 0x0a84ff]), alpha: 0.85 }),
            ];

            g.clear();
            cells.forEach((draw, i) => {
                g.save()
                    .translateTransform(40 + (i % 6) * CELL, 50 + Math.floor(i / 6) * 100)
                    .rotateTransform(a);
                draw(g);
                g.restore();
            });
        });

        return undefined;
    },
});
```

## Pick a renderer

`createSilkApp` creates a WebGL2 app. Pass `preference: 'webgpu'` to use WebGPU where the browser
has it:

```ts

const silk = await createSilkApp({ parent: document.body, preference: 'webgpu' });

silk.app.renderer.name; // 'webgpu', or 'webgl' where the browser has no WebGPU
silk.app.stage.addChild(new SilkGraphics().circle(60, 60, 40).fill(0x30d158));
```

Pixi tries WebGPU first and falls back to WebGL2. When it gets WebGPU, `createSilkApp` loads the
WGSL shader before it resolves.

WebGL2 stays the default because every current browser has it and it starts faster. Choose WebGPU
when the rest of your app needs it.

## Use WebGPU in your own Pixi app

The WGSL shader lives in its own entry point, `pixi-silk/webgpu`, so WebGL2 apps never download
it. If you create the application yourself, call `enableWebGPU()` once, before the first
`SilkGraphics`:

```ts

const app = new Application();

await app.init({ preference: 'webgpu' });
enableWebGPU();
app.stage.addChild(new SilkGraphics().circle(60, 60, 40).fill(0x30d158));
```

Objects created before the call have no WebGPU program. Pixi skips them and logs "Mesh shader has
no gpuProgram". Calling `enableWebGPU()` in a WebGL2 app does nothing harmful.

## Batch objects into one draw

Batching is off by default. Call `enableSilkBatching()` before you create the objects:

```ts

enableSilkBatching();
const dot = new SilkGraphics().circle(0, 0, 4).fill(0x0a84ff);
```

It works on WebGL2 and on WebGPU. On WebGPU it also needs `enableWebGPU()`, which `createSilkApp`
calls for you. [Performance](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/performance/#batch-many-objects) says what breaks a batch.

## Glass on both renderers

`Glass` from `pixi-silk/glass` reads the pixels behind it. On WebGL2 it reads the back buffer,
which it turns on the first time it draws. On WebGPU it copies the render target, so it needs no
back buffer.

## What differs

The two shaders are line-for-line ports. Three details differ because of the APIs:

| Detail | WebGL2 | WebGPU |
|---|---|---|
| Dither grain | rows counted from the bottom | rows counted from the top, so the grain is mirrored. Its strength is the same |
| Gradient ramp reads | the GPU's linear filter, which can round the blend weight to 8 bits | two exact texel loads, blended in the shader |
| Derivatives | `dFdx`, precision up to the GPU | `dpdx`, precision up to the GPU |

Edges can differ by a rounding step. Add `?renderer=webgpu` to a docs URL to run every demo on that
page on WebGPU.

---

# Resolution & DPR

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/resolution/
Section: Reference

> createSilkApp maps the canvas 1:1 to device pixels, even at fractional DPRs, follows DPR changes and renders filters at screen resolution.

`createSilkApp` gives you a canvas whose pixels are the screen's pixels. Exact edges need that as
much as they need the shader: if the browser rescales the canvas, every edge goes soft.

Live demo `resolution` (source):

```ts
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// A Siemens star is the hardest test for anti-aliasing: every wedge narrows below a pixel.
export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 240],
    controls: {
        resolution: { type: 'select', label: 'resolution', options: ['device', '1x', '2x', '3x'], value: 'device' },
    },
    setup({ silk, stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();
        let applied = '';

        stage.addChild(g);
        for (let i = 0; i < 36; i++) {
            const a = (i / 36) * Math.PI * 2;

            g.sector(240, 120, 110, a, a + Math.PI / 36).fill(0xffffff);
        }
        g.circle(240, 120, 110).stroke({ width: 1, color: 0x636366 });
        tick(() => {
            if (params.resolution === applied) return;
            applied = params.resolution;
            // createSilkApp sizes the backing store in device pixels; force 1x/2x/3x to compare
            silk.setResolution(applied === 'device' ? null : Number(applied[0]));
        });
    },
});
```

## Create a sharp canvas

```ts

const silk = await createSilkApp({
    parent: document.getElementById('stage')!,
    background: 0x000000,
    maxResolution: 3,
});

silk.app; // the Pixi Application
silk.width; // CSS pixels
silk.resolution; // device pixels per CSS pixel
silk.setResolution(1); // compare at 1x, null returns to devicePixelRatio
silk.destroy();
```

The canvas fills `parent`, so the parent needs a size. Every other option is a Pixi
`ApplicationOptions` field and passes through.

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `parent` | required | Element the canvas fills |
| `maxResolution` | `3` | Upper bound for the resolution, to cap memory and fill rate |
| `fixedResolution` | none | Forces a resolution instead of following `devicePixelRatio` |
| `onResize` | none | Called after every size or resolution change, with the size in CSS pixels |
| `inheritFilterResolution` | `true` | New Pixi filters render at the renderer resolution |
| `touchAction` | `'pan-y pinch-zoom'` | CSS `touch-action` of the canvas |
| `preference` | `'webgl'` | Renderer Pixi tries first. See [renderers](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/renderers/) |

## What it sets up

The backing store is sized from `devicePixelContentBoxSize`, so one canvas pixel is one device
pixel, even at a DPR of 1.5 or 2.625. Rounding `cssWidth * dpr` yourself can be off by one pixel.
The browser then resamples the whole canvas and blurs it. Safari has no device pixel box, so there
the size is rounded.

The canvas follows DPR changes, such as browser zoom or a move to another display.

MSAA is off (`antialias: false`), because the shader already computes coverage. Pixel rounding is
off too (`roundPixels: false`), so slow motion moves by fractions of a pixel instead of snapping.

Pixi filters render at resolution 1 by default, which blurs everything behind a filter on a retina
screen. `createSilkApp` sets `Filter.defaultOptions.resolution` to `'inherit'`. Turn that off with
`inheritFilterResolution: false`.

Pixi sets `touch-action: none` on its canvas, which stops the page from scrolling on phones. The
default here lets the page scroll. Use `touchAction: 'none'` for a canvas that handles drags
itself.

## Your own Application

If you create the application yourself, use the same settings:

```ts
await app.init({
    preference: 'webgl',
    antialias: false,
    autoDensity: true,
    resolution: window.devicePixelRatio,
    roundPixels: false,
});
Filter.defaultOptions.resolution = 'inherit';
```

This does not size the backing store to exact device pixels or follow DPR changes. For that, use
`createSilkApp` or copy its `ResizeObserver` code.

## Render textures and filters

A `SilkGraphics` in a render texture or behind a filter is anti-aliased at that target's
resolution. Give render textures the renderer's resolution to keep them sharp on retina screens.
The [render texture experiment](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/lab/06-render-texture/) shows the difference.

---

# Performance

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/performance/
Section: Reference

> What a SilkGraphics costs on the CPU and GPU, how batching joins objects into one draw, and how to keep static layers and large canvases cheap.

A `SilkGraphics` is one instanced draw call, whatever it contains. What you pay for is the CPU
work to rebuild it and the GPU work per covered pixel.

Live demo `stress` (source):

```ts
import { Text } from 'pixi.js';
import { SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// Everything is rebuilt every frame: one SilkGraphics, one draw call, however many primitives.
export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 260],
    controls: {
        count: { type: 'range', label: 'primitives', min: 500, max: 30000, step: 500, value: 5000 },
    },
    setup({ stage, params, tick }) {
        const g = new SilkGraphics();
        const stats = new Text({
            text: '',
            style: { fill: 0xffffff, fontSize: 12, fontFamily: 'ui-monospace, monospace' },
        });

        stats.position.set(12, 10);
        stage.addChild(g, stats);
        let cpu = 0;

        tick((t) => {
            const start = performance.now();

            g.clear();
            for (let i = 0; i < params.count; i++) {
                const a = i * 2.399963 + t * 0.2;
                const r = Math.sqrt(i / params.count) * 120;
                const x = 240 + Math.cos(a) * r * 1.8;
                const y = 130 + Math.sin(a) * r;

                if (i % 3 === 0) g.circle(x, y, 2.2).fill(0xff375f);
                else if (i % 3 === 1) g.roundRect(x - 2, y - 2, 4, 4, 1).fill(0x0a84ff);
                else g.line(x, y, x + 5, y + 2).stroke({ width: 1, color: 0x30d158 });
            }
            cpu = cpu * 0.9 + (performance.now() - start) * 0.1;
            stats.text = `${params.count} primitives, 1 draw call, rebuilt in ${cpu.toFixed(1)} ms`;
        });
    },
});
```

## The cost model

| Cost | What it is |
|---|---|
| Draw calls | One per `SilkGraphics`. With batching on, a run of them shares one |
| CPU | 44 floats per primitive, written into a reusable buffer when you redraw. Rebuilding 50,000 primitives every frame takes about 12 ms on a laptop. A UI with hundreds of primitives costs well under 0.5 ms |
| GPU | Each primitive is one quad sized to its bounds plus a one-pixel margin, shaded once per covered pixel. A blur grows the quad by three sigma |
| Memory | Buffers grow to the largest frame and stay. Gradients share one 256x256 half-float atlas, one row per ramp |

GPU cost follows covered area, like any 2D renderer. A full-screen blurred shape costs more than a
thousand small dots.

## Batch many objects

Batching is off by default. `enableSilkBatching()` turns it on for objects created after the call.

Live demo `batching` (source):

```ts
import { Container, Text, type WebGLRenderer } from 'pixi.js';
import { enableSilkBatching, SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';
import { defineDemo } from './runtime';

// 2000 separate SilkGraphics that move every frame. With batching on, runs of them share a draw,
// on WebGL2 and on WebGPU.
enableSilkBatching();

export default defineDemo({
    size: [480, 300],
    controls: {
        batching: { type: 'toggle', label: 'batching', value: true },
        count: { type: 'range', label: 'objects', min: 200, max: 4000, step: 200, value: 2000 },
    },
    setup({ silk, stage, params, tick }) {
        const layer = new Container();
        const caption = new Text({
            text: '',
            style: { fill: 0xffffff, fontSize: 12, fontFamily: 'ui-monospace, monospace' },
        });

        caption.position.set(12, 10);
        stage.addChild(layer, caption);

        // count draw calls: wrap the WebGL context, or the WebGPU render pass encoder
        const renderer = silk.app.renderer as WebGLRenderer;
        const gl = renderer.gl as WebGL2RenderingContext | undefined;
        const restore: (() => void)[] = [];
        let calls = 0;
        // only draws of this demo's renderer count: other demos on the page may draw in between
        let mine = false;
        const wrap = <T extends object>(target: T, names: (keyof T & string)[]) => {
            for (const name of names) {
                const fn = target[name] as unknown as (...a: unknown[]) => unknown;

                (target as Record<string, unknown>)[name] = function (this: unknown, ...a: unknown[]) {
                    if (mine) calls++;

                    return fn.apply(this, a);
                };
                restore.push(() => {
                    (target as Record<string, unknown>)[name] = fn;
                });
            }
        };

        if (gl) wrap(gl, ['drawElementsInstanced', 'drawElements']);
        else if (typeof GPURenderPassEncoder !== 'undefined')
            wrap(GPURenderPassEncoder.prototype, ['drawIndexed', 'draw']);
        const counter = {
            prerender: () => {
                calls = 0;
                mine = true;
            },
            postrender: () => {
                mine = false;
            },
        };

        silk.app.renderer.runners.prerender.add(counter);
        silk.app.renderer.runners.postrender.add(counter);

        let built = '';
        const colors = [0x0a84ff, 0x30d158, 0xff9f0a, 0xff375f, 0xbf5af2];
        const build = () => {
            for (const child of layer.removeChildren()) child.destroy();
            for (let i = 0; i < params.count; i++) {
                const g = new SilkGraphics({ batch: params.batching });
                const color = colors[i % colors.length];

                if (i % 3 === 0) g.circle(0, 0, 4).fill({ color, alpha: 0.8 });
                else if (i % 3 === 1) g.roundRect(-4, -4, 8, 8, 2).stroke({ width: 1.5, color });
                else g.star(0, 0, 5, 5).fill(color);
                layer.addChild(g);
            }
            built = `${params.batching}:${params.count}`;
        };

        tick((t) => {
            if (built !== `${params.batching}:${params.count}`) build();
            const n = layer.children.length;

            layer.children.forEach((g, i) => {
                const a = i * 2.399963 + t * 0.3;
                const r = Math.sqrt(i / n) * 130;

                g.position.set(240 + Math.cos(a) * r * 1.6, 150 + Math.sin(a) * r);
                g.rotation = t + i;
            });
            caption.text = `${n} objects, ${calls} draw calls last frame`;
        });

        return () => {
            for (const undo of restore) undo();
        };
    },
});
```

```ts

enableSilkBatching();
const dot = new SilkGraphics().circle(0, 0, 4).fill(0x0a84ff); // batched
const alone = new SilkGraphics({ batch: false }); // its own draw call
```

Consecutive `SilkGraphics` with the same blend mode and the same `dither`, `aaWidth` and
`minStrokePx` render in one draw. A filter, a mask, another kind of display object or a different
blend mode in between starts a new batch. Batching works on WebGL2 and on WebGPU.

A batch copies the instances and path data of its objects into one buffer. When none of them was
redrawn since the last frame, it copies only their matrices and tints.

## Keep frames cheap

Split static and dynamic parts. Draw backgrounds and fixed shapes once, and redraw only the parts
that change.

Move objects instead of redrawing them. Changing `position`, `rotation`, `scale` or `alpha` of a
`SilkGraphics` updates one matrix and costs nothing on the CPU side.

Create gradients once, at module scope. Identical ramps share an atlas row anyway, but reusing the
object skips parsing the stops again. The atlas has 256 rows. Past that, pixi-silk warns and reuses
row 0.

Put primitives that share a layer into one `SilkGraphics`, or turn on batching.

Cap the resolution of large canvases with `createSilkApp({ maxResolution: 2 })`. Fill rate grows
with the square of the resolution.

Stop redrawing when nothing moves. Check `Spring.settled`, or redraw only when the data changes.

---

# Glossary

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glossary/
Section: Reference

> Short definitions of anti-aliasing, MSAA, SSAA, FXAA, signed distance fields, coverage, device pixel ratio, squircles, OKLab, banding and dithering.

This page defines the terms used across these docs. Each entry starts with a one-sentence definition.

- **Aliasing** (jaggies, staircase artifacts): The jagged or crawling edges that appear when you sample a continuous shape at only one point per pixel. Each pixel is then either fully in or fully out.
- **Analytic anti-aliasing**: Anti-aliasing computed exactly per pixel from the shape's geometry, not from extra samples. pixi-silk derives coverage from the signed distance to the shape and the size of one device pixel.
- **Anti-aliasing** (antialiasing, AA): Techniques that remove the jagged "staircase" look of edges on a pixel grid. Each edge pixel gets a partial colour proportional to how much of it the shape covers.
- **Coverage**: The fraction of a pixel's area covered by a shape, from 0 to 1. Anti-aliasing uses coverage as the pixel's opacity along edges.
- **Device pixel**: One physical pixel of the display. A canvas is sharp only when each of its pixels maps to exactly one device pixel.
- **Device pixel ratio** (DPR, devicePixelRatio): The number of physical screen pixels per CSS pixel: 1 on standard displays, 2 or 3 on retina or HiDPI screens. Many laptops and phones have fractional ratios such as 1.25 or 1.5.
- **Dithering**: Adding a little structured noise (here ±½ of an 8-bit step) before quantising. It hides banding and leaves exact colours unchanged.
- **Draw call**: One command from the CPU telling the GPU to draw. Fewer draw calls usually mean better performance. Each SilkGraphics is one draw call.
- **FXAA** (fast approximate anti-aliasing): A cheap post-processing filter that detects and blurs high-contrast edges in the finished image. It softens detail and text and cannot recover geometry lost between pixels.
- **Gradient banding** (colour banding): Visible steps in a smooth gradient caused by 8-bit colour precision, most obvious in dark, wide gradients.
- **Hairline**: A line thinner than one device pixel. pixi-silk keeps hairlines one pixel wide and scales their opacity with their width, so they fade instead of breaking up.
- **Instanced rendering** (instancing): Drawing many copies of one mesh in a single draw call, each with its own data. pixi-silk draws every primitive of a SilkGraphics as one instance of a quad.
- **Monotone interpolation**: A curve through data points that never overshoots them. Peaks stay on the data and flat runs stay flat. pixi-silk uses Steffen's method (like d3's curveMonotoneX) for charts.
- **MSAA** (multisample anti-aliasing): A GPU technique that stores several coverage samples per pixel (typically 4) and averages them. In PixiJS, you enable it with antialias: true. By default it covers only the main canvas. Filters and render textures must opt in one by one.
- **OKLab**: A perceptual colour space by Björn Ottosson, where equal steps look equally different. Gradients interpolated in OKLab stay bright and even, without muddy midpoints.
- **Premultiplied alpha**: Storing colour already multiplied by opacity. Interpolating premultiplied colours prevents dark fringes when a gradient fades to transparent.
- **Signed distance field** (SDF): A function that returns the distance from any point to the nearest edge of a shape: negative inside, positive outside. Rendering a shape from its SDF gives exact edges at any scale.
- **Squircle** (superellipse corner, continuous corner): A rounded rectangle whose corners are superellipse arcs, so curvature grows gradually from the straight edge instead of jumping. iOS app icons and cards use it.
- **SSAA** (supersampling): Anti-aliasing by rendering at a higher resolution and downscaling. It is simple and high quality. Memory and fill-rate costs grow with the scale factor squared.
- **Tessellation**: Converting curves and shapes into triangles for the GPU. PixiJS Graphics tessellates when you draw, so curves become polygons with a fixed number of segments.

---

# How it works

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/how-it-works/
Section: Architecture

> One instanced quad per primitive, an exact signed distance per pixel, coverage from screen-space derivatives and dithered OKLab gradient ramps.

This page walks through the shader, from the instance buffer to the colour of one pixel. You do not
need it to use pixi-silk. Read it when you want to know why an edge, a join or a gradient looks the
way it does. [Anti-aliasing compared](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/anti-aliasing-compared/) sets the approach next to MSAA
and the other options.

## One instance per primitive

`SilkGraphics` is a Pixi `Mesh` that draws an instanced unit quad. Each primitive you add is one
instance of 44 floats, eleven `vec4` attributes:

| Attribute | Holds |
|---|---|
| `aBounds` | local bounds, including the stroke outset and three sigma of blur |
| `aShape0` to `aShape2` | the shape's parameters |
| `aMeta` | primitive type, flags, stroke width, blur sigma |
| `aFill`, `aStroke` | premultiplied colours |
| `aGrad`, `aPaint` | gradient geometry, kind, atlas row and extend mode |
| `aDash` | dash, gap, offset and stroke alignment |
| `aFx` | spread, progressive blur, and the object index when batched |

The vertex shader expands the quad to the bounds plus an anti-aliasing margin. The margin is in
device pixels. It uses the smallest singular value of the local-to-pixel Jacobian, so it stays right
at any zoom and for rotated or skewed objects.

## Exact distance, analytic coverage

For every pixel, the fragment shader computes the signed distance `d` from the pixel centre to the
shape, negative inside. Each primitive kind has its own exact function: rounded boxes with
per-corner radii and superellipse corners, ellipses, arcs, sectors, capsules, hearts, stars,
triangles and free paths. The shader turns the distance into coverage with a box filter one device
pixel wide:

```glsl
float px = sqrt(abs(dFdx(p).x * dFdy(p).y - dFdx(p).y * dFdy(p).x)); // one device pixel, in local units
float coverage = clamp(0.5 - d / px, 0.0, 1.0);
```

The one detail that matters is `px`. It comes from screen-space derivatives, so the filter is one
device pixel wide at 1000x zoom, when rotated, and inside filters and render textures. With `blur`,
the box filter becomes a gaussian, `0.5 - 0.5 * erf(d / (sigma * sqrt(2)))`. `spread` moves the
distance before the blur, which grows or shrinks the shape.

## Fill and stroke in one pass

A primitive with both a fill and a stroke is shaded once. The shader computes the coverage of the
whole shape and of the stroke band, and splits each pixel into stroke and fill outside the stroke.
No anti-aliased fill edge shows through an inner stroke.

## Paths

A stroked path is one distance field. Its segments sit in a float texture, and the shader takes the
nearest of their segments, caps and joins, the way Canvas 2D defines a stroke. Joins are miter (the
default, cut to a bevel past `miterLimit`), bevel or round. Every pixel is shaded once, so a
translucent path never blends twice where it overlaps itself.

Long subpaths are split into chunks of 32 segments. Each chunk also checks the segments of other
chunks that come near it, found on the CPU. A pixel goes to the chunk with the nearest segment, so
it is shaded once even where the path crosses itself.

A filled path stores its edges the same way. The distance is the nearest edge, and the sign comes
from even-odd crossings. Tapered strokes keep one instance per segment, with the exact distance to
a capsule whose ends have different radii.

## Unions and shape operations

`union: true` on a fill or stroke stores every shape of the path as a record in the path texture.
The shader takes the nearest distance, so overlapping shapes paint as one.

[Shape operations](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/shape-operations/) use the same records, each with an op. The shader folds
them on a small stack. The minimum of two distances is a union and the maximum an intersection.
`max(a, -b)` subtracts b from a, and `max(min(a, b), -max(a, b))` excludes. All four are exact on
the outline.

## Areas

Chart areas are split into vertical columns that tile exactly. Shared column edges get no
anti-aliasing margin. Only the top and bottom edges do, so a translucent fill has no seams.

## Hairlines

A stroke thinner than `minStrokePx` (one device pixel by default) is drawn at that width, with its
alpha scaled down by the ratio. The amount of ink stays the same, and thin lines never break into
dots.

## Gradients

Stops are interpolated premultiplied, in OKLab by default, and baked into a shared 256x256 RGBA16F
atlas, one reference-counted row per ramp. The shader adds plus or minus half an 8-bit step of
interleaved gradient noise to gradients and blurs. That removes banding and leaves exact 8-bit
colours alone. `dither: 0` turns it off.

## Batching

With `enableSilkBatching()`, consecutive objects copy their instances into one buffer. Each
instance carries its object index in `aFx.w`. The vertex shader reads that object's matrix, tint and
path texel base from a small table texture. [Performance](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/performance/) covers when a batch
breaks.

## Hit testing

The same distance functions run on the CPU. `containsPoint` tests the real shape, holes and stroke
widths included. [Interaction and motion](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/interaction-and-motion/) shows it in use.

## WebGPU

The WGSL shader is a line-for-line port of the GLSL one. [Renderers](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/renderers/) lists the
small differences.

---

# Anti-aliasing compared

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/anti-aliasing-compared/
Section: Architecture

> MSAA, resolution, curve smoothness, supersampling, FXAA, @pixi/graphics-smooth and analytic SDF anti-aliasing in PixiJS v8, compared, with fixes by symptom.

Anti-aliasing gives each edge pixel a partial colour, in proportion to how much of it the shape
covers. PixiJS v8 offers five ways to get there. pixi-silk adds a sixth: it computes coverage from
each shape's exact signed distance, per pixel. That is what the rest of the docs mean when they say
an edge stays sharp at any zoom, rotation and device pixel ratio.

## The options at a glance

| Technique | How to turn it on in PixiJS v8 | Edge quality | Cost | Applies to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MSAA | `app.init({ antialias: true })` | 4 samples, so 5 coverage levels per edge pixel | memory bandwidth, a resolve pass | the main canvas. Render textures and filters opt in |
| Higher resolution | `resolution: devicePixelRatio, autoDensity: true` | smaller stairs, still aliased | fill rate grows with DPR squared | everything |
| Curve smoothness | `app.init({ bezierSmoothness: 0.9 })` | fewer facets on curves, edges still aliased | more triangles | Graphics curves |
| Supersampling | draw into a 2x render texture, then draw it scaled down | high | 4x the pixels and an extra texture | what you draw into it |
| FXAA | a post-process filter | softer edges, blurred detail and text | one full-screen pass | the filtered object |
| Analytic SDF (pixi-silk) | `new SilkGraphics()` | exact coverage, continuous | one instanced draw call per object | everywhere, filters and render textures included |

## MSAA in PixiJS v8

```ts

const app = new Application();

await app.init({
    antialias: true, // MSAA on the main canvas
    resolution: window.devicePixelRatio,
    autoDensity: true,
});
```

MSAA belongs to a render target, so it does not follow your objects. Render textures are not
multisampled unless you create them with `antialias: true`. Filters render into their own targets
without MSAA and at resolution 1, unless you change both.

MSAA works for large shapes at rest. UI and charts show where it stops:

- Slowly moving or rotating edges jump between the five coverage levels, which reads as shimmer.
- Lines thinner than a pixel fall between the four samples and look dotted.
- Zooming in shows the facets of curves, because Graphics fixed its triangles when you drew them.

## Analytic anti-aliasing

A signed distance field gives the distance from any point to the shape's edge. pixi-silk evaluates
each primitive's exact distance per pixel and turns it into coverage over one device pixel:

```glsl
float px = sqrt(abs(dFdx(p).x * dFdy(p).y - dFdx(p).y * dFdy(p).x)); // one device pixel, in shape units
float coverage = clamp(0.5 - d / px, 0.0, 1.0); // d: signed distance to the edge
```

The pixel size comes from screen-space derivatives. So the result holds at any scale, rotation,
resolution and render target, with nothing to tessellate and no samples to miss. Each
`SilkGraphics` draws all its primitives in one instanced call. [How it works](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/how-it-works/)
follows the shader step by step.

```ts

const { app } = await createSilkApp({ parent: document.body });
const g = new SilkGraphics();

g.circle(200, 150, 80).stroke({ width: 2, color: 0x64d2ff });
g.roundRect(100, 60, 200, 180, 40, 0.6).stroke({ width: 0.5, color: 0xffffff });
app.stage.addChild(g);
```

The circle is exact at any zoom. The half-pixel stroke is drawn one pixel wide at half the alpha,
so it never breaks up. `createSilkApp` keeps MSAA off, because it would only cost bandwidth.

Analytic anti-aliasing has limits too. It applies to what `SilkGraphics` draws, not to sprites or
Pixi `Graphics`. GPU cost follows covered area, so a large blurred shape costs more than many small
ones.

## Fix a symptom

Most of these fixes work with plain `Graphics`. The last column is the pixi-silk route.

| You see | Cause | Fix in PixiJS | With pixi-silk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jagged, stair-stepped edges | `antialias` is `false` by default | `app.init({ antialias: true })` | `SilkGraphics` computes coverage itself |
| Circles look like polygons when zoomed | Graphics cuts curves into segments when you draw | raise `bezierSmoothness`, or redraw at the final scale | curves are evaluated per pixel |
| Thin lines flicker, look dotted or vanish | a sub-pixel line covers a fraction of each pixel, and samples miss it | keep strokes at least one device pixel wide | hairlines fade instead of thinning. See [strokes and dashes](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/strokes-and-dashes/) |
| Everything is a little blurry on retina screens | the canvas has fewer pixels than the screen, or was rounded at a fractional DPR | `resolution: devicePixelRatio, autoDensity: true` | `createSilkApp` maps canvas pixels 1:1. See [resolution](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/resolution/) |
| Content behind a filter is blurry | filters render at resolution 1 | `Filter.defaultOptions.resolution = 'inherit'` | `createSilkApp` sets it for you |
| Gradients show bands | 8-bit colour, with no dither in `FillGradient` | none built in | half-float ramps, OKLab and dither. See [gradients](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/gradients/) |
| Slow motion snaps from pixel to pixel | `roundPixels: true` | keep `roundPixels: false` | the default in `createSilkApp` |

## @pixi/graphics-smooth on PixiJS v8

[`@pixi/graphics-smooth`](https://github.com/pixijs-userland/graphics-smooth) is the community
plugin that made v7 `Graphics` smooth. Its `SmoothGraphics` class anti-aliases in the shader,
without MSAA. Its 1.1 line requires PixiJS 7.2 or a newer v7, and as of September 2026 there is no
v8 release on npm. On v8, `SilkGraphics` fills that role with a v8-style API.

```ts nocheck
// PixiJS v7 + @pixi/graphics-smooth
const g = new SmoothGraphics();
g.lineStyle({ width: 2, color: 0xffffff });
g.beginFill(0x1c1c1e);
g.drawRoundedRect(0, 0, 200, 80, 16);
g.endFill();
g.drawCircle(40, 40, 12);
```

```ts
// PixiJS v8 + pixi-silk
const g = new SilkGraphics();
g.roundRect(0, 0, 200, 80, 16).fill(0x1c1c1e).stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xffffff });
g.circle(40, 40, 12).stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xffffff });
```

| v7 call | SilkGraphics |
|---|---|
| `beginFill(c, a)` to `endFill()` | `shape().fill({ color: c, alpha: a })` |
| `lineStyle({ width, color, alpha })` | `shape().stroke({ width, color, alpha })` |
| `drawRect`, `drawRoundedRect`, `drawCircle`, `drawEllipse` | `rect`, `roundRect`, `circle`, `ellipse` |
| `moveTo`, `lineTo`, `bezierCurveTo` | the same, then `fill()` or `stroke()` |
| `arc(...)` | `arc(...)`, which starts its own subpath, or `arcSweep(...)` |
| `LINE_SCALE_MODE.NONE` | not built in. Divide the width by the scale |

PixiJS v8 changed the Graphics API itself. The [PixiJS v8 migration guide](https://pixijs.com/8.x/guides/migrations/v8)
covers the upgrade, and [migrating from Graphics](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/migrating-from-graphics/) covers how v8
`Graphics` and `SilkGraphics` differ.

## Which one to use

For sprites and textures only, skip MSAA. The GPU filters textures already.

For a few large shapes and no zoom, `antialias: true` with `resolution: devicePixelRatio` is
enough.

For UI, charts, icons, thin lines and vector content that zooms or rotates, use `SilkGraphics` and
keep `antialias: false`. The same holds for content behind filters or in render textures.

The [infinite zoom](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/lab/03-zoom/) and [sub-pixel motion](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/lab/04-subpixel/) experiments at the end
of this page show the difference full screen.

## References

- PixiJS v8 [Graphics API](https://pixijs.download/release/docs/scene.Graphics.html) and the
  [issue on smoother curves in v8](https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/issues/9831).
- Inigo Quilez, [2D distance functions](https://iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d/).
- web.dev, [pixel-perfect rendering with devicePixelContentBox](https://web.dev/articles/device-pixel-content-box).
- Glossary: [MSAA](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glossary/#msaa), [SSAA](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glossary/#ssaa), [FXAA](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glossary/#fxaa)
  and [signed distance field](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/glossary/#signed-distance-field).

# Layout engine

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/layout-engine/
Section: Architecture

> pixi-silk/layout is the flex engine under SmartContainer and FlexContainer: plain nodes, CSS flexbox styles, measure functions and incremental passes.

`pixi-silk/layout` lays out a tree of plain nodes with CSS flexbox. It has no Pixi in it, so it
runs in tests, workers and on a server. [Layout](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/docs/layout/) wraps it in Pixi containers.
Read this page when you want the engine without Pixi, or need to know why a box ended up where it did.

## Lay out a tree

```ts

const root = new LayoutNode({ direction: 'row', gap: 8, padding: 16 });
const icon = new LayoutNode({ width: 100 });
const label = new LayoutNode({ grow: 1 });

root.add(icon).add(label);
root.calculate(400, 120);

label.layout; // { x: 124, y: 16, width: 260, height: 88 }
```

The label starts after the padding, the icon and the gap (16 + 100 + 8), takes the rest of the
width and stretches to the content height. `calculate(width, height)` lays out the whole tree, and
each node's `layout` holds its box relative to its parent. Leave a size out to fit that axis to
the content.

A node has a style, children and an optional `measure` function. `setStyle()` replaces the style
and `updateStyle()` merges into it. `add()`, `remove()` and `clear()` change the children.

## Styles

The style follows CSS flexbox, with `box-sizing: border-box` everywhere and shorter names.
Alignment values are `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch` and, for items, `baseline`.

| Group | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| Container | `direction` (`row`, `column` and their `-reverse`), `wrap`, `gap`, `rowGap`, `columnGap`, `padding`, `justifyContent`, `alignItems`, `alignContent` |
| Item | `grow` (0), `shrink` (1), `basis` (`auto`), `alignSelf`, `margin` |
| Size | `width`, `height`, `minWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxWidth`, `maxHeight`, `aspectRatio` |
| Position | `position: 'absolute'` with `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left` or `inset`, and `display: 'none'` |

Sizes are pixels, a percent of the parent's content box such as `'50%'`, or `'auto'`. Padding and
margin take one value, or two, three or four as in CSS. An `auto` margin takes the free space,
which centres an item or pushes it to the far end. Anchors of absolute items may be percents.

## How a pass computes

Each container first works out the basis of its items: the `basis`, else the `width` or `height`,
else the measured content. It breaks items into lines when `wrap` is on, then shares out the free
space of each line.

Grow and shrink run the CSS loop. Items that hit their `min` or `max` freeze there, and the rest
of the space goes round again until nothing changes. Shrinking is weighted by the basis, as in a
browser, so a wide item gives up more than a narrow one.

Then the cross axis. Lines are placed by `alignContent`, and items in a line by `alignItems` or
their `alignSelf`. A stretched item gets the line's cross size and lays out its own children
again at that size.

## Measure content

A leaf with content, such as text or a sprite, gets a `measure` function. It receives the space
offered and returns the content size, without padding. Either argument is `Infinity` when that
axis is free.

```ts

const charWidth = 9;
const lineHeight = 20;
const copy = 'Tap a card to open it in full view';

const text = new LayoutNode({}, (availableWidth) => {
    const perLine = Math.max(1, Math.floor(availableWidth / charWidth));
    const lines = Math.ceil(copy.length / perLine);

    return { width: Math.min(copy.length, perLine) * charWidth, height: lines * lineHeight };
});

new LayoutNode({ direction: 'column', width: 160 }).add(text).calculate();
```

In a 160-wide column the copy wraps at 17 characters a line, so the function returns 153 by 40.
The column then stretches the node to its full width of 160. Return a
`baseline` too, the distance from the top to the first baseline, and `alignItems: 'baseline'`
lines up text in a row.

## Incremental passes

Changing a style, adding or removing a child, or calling `markDirty()` marks the node and its
ancestors dirty. The next `calculate()` skips every clean subtree whose space did not change. A
measured leaf caches its size per available space, so it is measured again only after
`markDirty()`. Call it when the text or texture behind a leaf changes.

## Differences from CSS

The engine follows CSS where results differ in practice. A few things are simpler.

| Topic | What the engine does |
| --- | --- |
| Minimum size | An item's default minimum is 0, not its content size. Set `minWidth` or `shrink: 0` to keep it from shrinking below its content |
| Aspect ratio | A stretched cross size wins over `aspectRatio`, as in CSS. Set `alignSelf` to keep the ratio |
| Baseline | A container's baseline is its first item's. Only measured leaves report one of their own |
| Absolute items | Without anchors they sit where `justifyContent` and `alignItems` put them, not at their static position |
| Not there | `order`, `overflow`, borders and `flex-basis: content` |

The engine knows nothing about transforms. FlexContainer measures rotated children unrotated and
gives them their box as if they were not rotated.

---

## GradientAtlas (Class)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/GradientAtlas/

All gradient ramps live in one RGBA16F texture (one ramp per row), shared by every
SilkGraphics. Half floats keep ~11 bits per channel so dark and low-alpha ramps
don't get quantised before the shader dithers them to the 8-bit framebuffer.

## SilkGraphics (Class)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/SilkGraphics/

A PixiJS display object with a `Graphics`-like API. Every primitive is a signed distance field
evaluated per pixel, so edges are smooth at any scale, rotation and device pixel ratio. Each
object is one instanced draw call.

Shapes go on the active path and are painted by [fill()](#fill) or
[stroke()](#stroke). `stroke()` right after `fill()` paints the same shapes.
Redrawing every frame is cheap, because [clear()](#clear) keeps the buffers.

## Example

```ts
const g = new SilkGraphics()
    .roundRect(0, 0, 160, 80, 20, 0.6).fill(0x1c1c1e)
    .arc(80, 40, 28, -Math.PI / 2, Math.PI).stroke({ width: 8, cap: 'round', color: 0x30d158 });
app.stage.addChild(g);
```

## Extends

- `Mesh`\<[`SilkGeometry`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/SilkGeometry/), `Shader`\>

## Constructors

### Constructor

```ts
new SilkGraphics(options?: SilkGraphicsOptions): SilkGraphics;
```

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`SilkGraphicsOptions`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/SilkGraphicsOptions/) |

#### Returns

`SilkGraphics`

#### Overrides

```ts
Mesh<SilkGeometry, Shader>.constructor
```

## Properties

| Property | Modifier | Type | Description | Defined in |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
|  `defaults` | `static` | `Required`\<`Omit`\<[`SilkGraphicsOptions`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/SilkGraphicsOptions/), `"label"` \| `"batch"`\>\> | Settings for new objects. Change them before you create any SilkGraphics. | SilkGraphics.ts:620 |

### boolean()

```ts
boolean(
   op: ShapeOp, 
   a: (g: this) => unknown, 
   b: (g: this) => unknown
): this;
```

Adds one shape to the active path: what `a` draws combined with what `b` draws by `op`. The
shapes each callback adds are merged first, and a callback can call `boolean()` again to nest.
Paint the result with `fill()` or `stroke()` like any shape. The callbacks only add shapes:
do not paint inside them.

The outline is exact, so anti-aliasing is as sharp as on a circle. Inside the shape the
distance is a close bound, not exact: a large blur, spread or inner shadow can round its
inner corners slightly.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `op` | [`ShapeOp`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/ShapeOp/) |
| `a` | (`g`: `this`) => `unknown` |
| `b` | (`g`: `this`) => `unknown` |

#### Returns

`this`

#### Example

```ts
// a ring with a notch: a circle minus a smaller circle and a bar
g.boolean('subtract', (g) => g.circle(50, 50, 40), (g) => g.circle(50, 50, 24).rect(46, 0, 8, 30))
    .fill(0x30d158)
    .stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xffffff });
```

***

## SilkPipe (Class)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/SilkPipe/

and WebGPU. [enableSilkBatching](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/enableSilkBatching/) installs it.

## createSilkApp (Function)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/createSilkApp/

```ts
function createSilkApp(options: SilkAppOptions): Promise<SilkApp>;
```

Creates a Pixi application tuned for smooth vector output:

- WebGL2 by default, WebGPU with `preference: 'webgpu'` (the WGSL shader then loads on demand),
- no MSAA (analytic AA does the job, MSAA would only cost bandwidth),
- backing store sized from `devicePixelContentBoxSize`, so every canvas pixel maps to
  exactly one device pixel even at fractional DPRs (1.25, 1.5, 2.625 ...) - no resampling blur,
- follows DPR changes (moving the window between displays, browser zoom),
- unrounded coordinates for sub-pixel smooth motion,
- filters that render at the screen resolution instead of 1x.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`SilkAppOptions`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/SilkAppOptions/) |

## Returns

`Promise`\<[`SilkApp`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/SilkApp/)\>

## damp (Function)

function damp(
   current: number, 
   target: number, 
   lambda: number,

Exponential approach: moves `current` towards `target`. `lambda` is about 1/seconds, higher is snappier.

## enableSilkBatching (Function)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/enableSilkBatching/

```ts
function enableSilkBatching(): void;
```

Turns on batching across objects: runs of consecutive SilkGraphics with the same blend mode and
settings render in one draw call. Objects created after the call take part. Each renderer gets
the pipe the first time it draws one of them, so you can call it before or after creating the
Application. It is safe to call again.

It works with WebGL2 and with WebGPU. On WebGPU, call `enableWebGPU()` too ([createSilkApp](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/createSilkApp/)
does it for you), or objects draw one call each, as without batching.

## Returns

`void`

## Example

```ts
import { enableSilkBatching, SilkGraphics } from 'pixi-silk';

enableSilkBatching();
const app = new Application();
await app.init();
```

## mesh (Function)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/mesh/

```ts
function mesh(
   cols: number, 
   rows: number, 
   colors: MeshColorInput[], 
   options?: MeshGradientOptions
): MeshGradient;
```

Gradient mesh: `cols` x `rows` control colours (row by row, top-left first) spread over the
painted shape's box, blended into one smooth surface.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `cols` | `number` |
| `rows` | `number` |
| `colors` | [`MeshColorInput`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/MeshColorInput/)[] |
| `options` | [`MeshGradientOptions`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/MeshGradientOptions/) |

## Returns

[`MeshGradient`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/MeshGradient/)

## Example

```ts
// a light beam that fades at the sides and towards the top
const beam = mesh(3, 3, [
    [0xffd6e8, 0], [0xffd6e8, 0], [0xffd6e8, 0],
    [0xffd6e8, 0.2], [0xffd6e8, 0.5], [0xffd6e8, 0.2],
    [0xffe6f0, 0.6], [0xffffff, 1], [0xffe6f0, 0.6],
]);
g.rect(0, 0, 200, 240).fill(beam);
```

## monotoneX (Function)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/monotoneX/

```ts
function monotoneX(flat: number[], step?: number): number[];
```

Monotone cubic interpolation in x (Steffen's method, same family as d3's monotoneX).
Never overshoots the data: peaks stay at the data points, flat runs stay flat.
`step` is the target spacing of the output samples in local units.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default value |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `flat` | `number`[] | `undefined` |
| `step` | `number` | `2` |

## Returns

`number`[]

|  `color?` | `ColorSource` | Colour, any Pixi `ColorSource`. With a gradient, it tints the gradient. | SilkGraphics.ts:82 |
|  `gradient?` | [`Gradient`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/Gradient/) | Gradient paint. `color` (if given) tints it. | SilkGraphics.ts:86 |
|  `innerShadow?` | [`InnerShadow`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/InnerShadow/) \| [`InnerShadow`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/InnerShadow/)[] | One or more shadows inside closed shapes, drawn in order on top of the fill. | SilkGraphics.ts:100 |
|  `op?` | [`ShapeOp`](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/ShapeOp/) | Combines the closed shapes of the active path into one shape, exact on its outline. `subtract` takes every later shape out of the first one, `intersect` keeps what they all cover, and `exclude` keeps what an odd number of them cover. `union` is the same as `union: true`. A path from `moveTo()` or `svgPath()` takes part as one shape, even-odd. With `stroke()`, the stroke follows the outline of the result. See [SilkGraphics.boolean](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/classes/SilkGraphics/#boolean) for nested operations. Default none: every shape is painted on its own. | SilkGraphics.ts:117 |
|  `spread?` | `number` | Grows the shape by this many local units before it is blurred, like a Figma shadow spread. Negative shrinks it. | SilkGraphics.ts:93 |
|  `union?` | `boolean` | Paints every closed shape of the active path as one shape: their distance fields merge, so overlaps are painted once and blur, anti-aliasing and opacity show no seam where they meet. Polygons from `poly()` and `moveTo()` join in too, each subpath on its own. With `stroke()`, the stroke follows the outline of the union, and open paths merge into one stroke. Default false. | SilkGraphics.ts:108 |

## InnerShadow (Interface)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/InnerShadow/

A shadow drawn inside the shape from its own distance field, with Figma's semantics. The shape is
moved by `x` and `y`, shrunk by `spread` and blurred. What it no longer covers is shaded.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description | Defined in |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
|  `alpha?` | `number` | Opacity from 0 to 1. Default 1. | SilkGraphics.ts:66 |
|  `blend?` | `"normal"` \| `"add"` | `add` paints it plus-lighter: it brightens what is underneath. Default `normal`. | SilkGraphics.ts:76 |
|  `blur?` | `number` | Blur (standard deviation, local units). Default 0. | SilkGraphics.ts:72 |
|  `color?` | `ColorSource` | Colour, any Pixi `ColorSource`. Default black. | SilkGraphics.ts:64 |
|  `spread?` | `number` | Grows the shadow inwards. Negative values make it thinner. Default 0. | SilkGraphics.ts:74 |
|  `x?` | `number` | Horizontal offset, local units. Positive moves the shadow right. Default 0. | SilkGraphics.ts:68 |
|  `y?` | `number` | Vertical offset, local units. Positive moves the shadow down. Default 0. | SilkGraphics.ts:70 |

|  `width` | `readonly` | `number` | Current width in CSS pixels. | app.ts:37 |

## Methods

### destroy()

```ts
destroy(): void;
```

Stops observers, destroys the stage and renderer and removes the canvas. Safe with several apps on a page.

#### Returns

`void`

***

### setResolution()

```ts
setResolution(resolution: number | null): void;
```

Forces a resolution, for example to compare 1x and 2x. `null` returns to devicePixelRatio.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `resolution` | `number` \| `null` |

#### Returns

`void`

## ColorSpace (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/ColorSpace/

```ts
type ColorSpace = "oklab" | "srgb" | "linear";
```

Colour space gradients are interpolated in: perceptual OKLab (default), linear light, or plain sRGB.

## Easing (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/Easing/

```ts
type Easing = "linear" | "smooth" | ((t: number) => number);
```

How the ramp moves between stops.

- `linear`: piecewise linear between stops (CSS behaviour).
- `smooth`: monotone cubic spline through the stops with eased ends. Removes the
  Mach bands you see at every stop of a linear ramp and never overshoots.
- a function remaps the gradient parameter before lookup (e.g. an easing curve for scrims).

## ExtendMode (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/ExtendMode/

```ts
type ExtendMode = "pad" | "repeat" | "reflect";
```

What a gradient does outside 0..1: hold the end colours (`pad`), tile (`repeat`) or mirror (`reflect`).

## FillInput (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/FillInput/

```ts
type FillInput = 
  | ColorSource
  | Gradient
  | FillStyle;
```

What `fill()` accepts: any Pixi colour, a gradient or a [FillStyle](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/FillStyle/).

## GradientUnits (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/GradientUnits/

```ts
type GradientUnits = "shape" | "local";
```

Gradient coordinates: `shape` = fractions of each painted shape's box, `local` = the graphics' local units (one ramp across many shapes).

## LineCap (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/LineCap/

```ts
type LineCap = "butt" | "round" | "square";
```

Shape of the ends of open paths and of every dash: flat, round or square.

## LineJoin (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/LineJoin/

```ts
type LineJoin = "miter" | "bevel" | "round";
```

Shape of the corners where two segments of a stroke meet.

## MeshColorInput (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/MeshColorInput/

```ts
type MeshColorInput = ColorSource | [ColorSource, number];
```

A mesh control colour: any Pixi colour, or `[color, alpha]`.

## PointsInput (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/PointsInput/

```ts
type PointsInput = number[] | Float32Array | Float64Array | PointData[];
```

Points as a flat `[x0, y0, x1, y1, ...]` array, a typed array, or an array of `{ x, y }` objects.

## RGBA (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/RGBA/

```ts
type RGBA = [number, number, number, number];
```

Straight (non-premultiplied) sRGB colour with alpha, all channels 0..1, as returned by [parseColor](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/functions/parseColor/).

## ShapeOp (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/ShapeOp/

```ts
type ShapeOp = "union" | "subtract" | "intersect" | "exclude";
```

A shape operation: `union` merges, `subtract` cuts the later shapes out of the first,
`intersect` keeps the overlap, and `exclude` keeps what is covered an odd number of times.

## StopInput (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/StopInput/

```ts
type StopInput = 
  | ColorSource
  | [number, ColorSource]
  | [number, ColorSource, number]
  | {
  alpha?: number;
  color: ColorSource;
  offset: number;
};
```

A color stop: a bare color (stops are spread evenly), `[offset, color]`,
`[offset, color, alpha]` or `{ offset, color, alpha }`.

## StrokeInput (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/StrokeInput/

```ts
type StrokeInput = 
  | ColorSource
  | Gradient
  | StrokeStyle;
```

What `stroke()` accepts: any Pixi colour, a gradient or a [StrokeStyle](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/interfaces/StrokeStyle/).

## Vec2 (Type)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/types/Vec2/

```ts
type Vec2 = [number, number];
```

A point `[x, y]`. In `shape` units, x and y are fractions of the painted shape's box.

## ease (Variable)

URL: https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev/api/variables/ease/

```ts
const ease: {
  inOutCubic: (t: number) => number;
  inOutSine: (t: number) => number;
  outCubic: (t: number) => number;
  outExpo: (t: number) => number;
};
```

Easing curves for tweens (t from 0 to 1): inOutCubic, outCubic, inOutSine, outExpo.

|  `outExpo()` | (`t`: `number`) => `number` | Sharp start, long soft landing. | motion.ts:76 |

# FAQ

## What is pixi-silk?

An MIT-licensed TypeScript library for PixiJS v8. Its `SilkGraphics` display object has a Graphics-like API and draws each shape as a distance field, anti-aliased per pixel in the shader.

## Is pixi-silk a replacement for Graphics?

For UI, chart and icon drawing, yes: `SilkGraphics` keeps the active path, `fill()` and `stroke()`. It has no texture fills and no `svg()` import (`svgPath(d)` reads one path string), and both classes work side by side.

## Which entry point do I import?

The root `pixi-silk` import holds SilkGraphics, gradients, `createSilkApp` and batching. Text, layout, glass, glow, WebGPU and every UI widget are separate entry points, such as `pixi-silk/text` or `pixi-silk/ui/gizmo`, so an app bundles only what it imports.

## Can I use pixi-silk in React, Vue or Svelte?

Yes. Create the app in a mount hook with `createSilkApp({ parent: element })` and call its `destroy()` on unmount.

## What license is pixi-silk under?

MIT, for commercial and open-source use.

## How do I draw a squircle (iOS-style rounded rectangle) in PixiJS?

Call `g.roundRect(x, y, width, height, radius, smoothing)` with smoothing between 0 and 1. iOS uses about 0.6.

## Why do thin lines flicker or disappear in PixiJS?

A line thinner than one device pixel covers only part of each pixel, so sampling hits some pixels and misses others. SilkGraphics keeps such hairlines one pixel wide and lowers their opacity with their width.

## Can SilkGraphics fill a free-form path?

Yes. A path from `moveTo()`, `lineTo()`, the curve calls or `svgPath(d)` fills with the even-odd rule and strokes with miter, bevel or round joins.

## How do I cut one shape out of another?

Use `g.boolean('subtract', a, b)` with two callbacks that draw the shapes, or pass `op` to `fill()`. Union, intersect, subtract and exclude are supported.

## How do I make gradients in PixiJS without banding?

Fill with `linear`, `radial`, `conic` or `along` from pixi-silk. Gradients are baked into a half-float atlas and dithered by half an 8-bit step, which hides the bands in dark, wide ramps.

## How do I add a glow or soft shadow without a filter?

Give the paint a `blur`, for example `g.circle(0, 0, 40).fill({ color: 0xff375f, blur: 12 })`. Add `spread` to grow the shape before the blur.

## Are glass and glow part of the root import?

No. Glass lives in `pixi-silk/glass` and glow in `pixi-silk/glow`. Both are filters, so they cost a render pass where plain blur does not.

## Why is PixiJS Text blurry when I zoom in?

PixiJS `Text` is a bitmap, so scaling it stretches its pixels. `SilkText` from `pixi-silk/text` draws glyphs from a distance field atlas and keeps its edges under a zooming camera.

## Which scripts does SilkText support?

Latin, Greek and Cyrillic UI text. There is no shaping, so right-to-left text, ligatures and combining marks do not work, and emoji come out as one-colour silhouettes. Use PixiJS `Text` for those.

## Do IME and mobile keyboards work in the text editor?

`TextEditor` types through a hidden `<textarea>` that follows the caret, so input methods, mobile keyboards, autocorrect and the clipboard work. Spell check underlines do not show.

## Do pointer events work on SilkGraphics?

Yes. Set `eventMode = 'static'` and listen as usual. Hit tests use the real shapes, so a stroked circle is hollow and a line reacts only within its stroke width.

## Why does my SmartContainer not move or scale?

It needs a `viewport`: pass the Pixi `Application`, a signal or a rectangle as `viewport` or call `setViewport()`. Without one it has no window to place itself in.

## How close is the layout engine to CSS flexbox?

It follows flexbox for direction, wrap, grow, shrink, gaps and alignment. It has no `order`, `overflow` or borders, and an item's default minimum size is 0, not its content size.

## How do I animate a counter or a balance?

Use `Odometer` from `pixi-silk/ui/odometer`. `set(value)` rolls each digit column to the new value, and `skip()` jumps to the end.

## Is the editor kit stable?

No. The editor kit is experimental in 1.0, and its API may change in a minor release.

## Does the editor kit keep my document?

No. The widgets draw and report. You keep the document, and `pixi-silk/selection` and `pixi-silk/history` hold the selection and the undo stack if you want them.

## Do I need DOM panels over the canvas for a scene editor?

No. `pixi-silk/ui/panel` draws dockable panels on the canvas, and `layers`, `inspector` and `minimap` fill them. They are Pixi containers, so they share the scene, its pointer events and its undo history.

## How do I draw charts with PixiJS?

Use `area(points, baseline, { smooth: 'monotone' })` for filled areas, `polyline` for lines and `roundRect` for bars. Monotone smoothing never overshoots the data.

## Can I copy the showcase widgets into my app?

Yes, they are MIT like the library. They are site code, not exports, so copy the lab file you need from the repository.

## Does pixi-silk work with WebGPU?

Yes. Pass `preference: 'webgpu'` to `createSilkApp`, or call `enableWebGPU()` from `pixi-silk/webgpu` before the first SilkGraphics in your own Pixi app. WebGL2 is the default and the fallback.

## How do I draw many SilkGraphics in one draw call?

Call `enableSilkBatching()` before you create the objects. It is off by default and works on WebGL2 and WebGPU. Without it, each SilkGraphics is one instanced draw call.

## Why is my PixiJS canvas blurry on retina or high-DPI screens?

The canvas backing store does not match the device pixels, or a filter renders at resolution 1. `createSilkApp` sizes the canvas from `devicePixelContentBoxSize` and makes filters inherit the screen resolution.

## Does pixi-silk need antialias: true?

No. Coverage is computed per pixel, so create the app with `antialias: false`, as `createSilkApp` does. MSAA would only cost memory bandwidth.

## How do I enable anti-aliasing in PixiJS v8?

Pass `antialias: true` to `app.init()` for MSAA on the main canvas, with `resolution: window.devicePixelRatio` and `autoDensity: true` for retina screens. MSAA skips filters and render textures unless you opt them in.

## Why do PixiJS v8 Graphics look jagged or blurry?

Graphics are tessellated into triangles, and only MSAA smooths their edges. Scaled curves show facets, thin lines crawl between pixels, and filters render at resolution 1 by default.

## What is analytic anti-aliasing?

Each edge pixel's coverage is computed from the shape's geometry, not from a few samples. pixi-silk divides the signed distance to the shape by the size of one device pixel.

## Is there a PixiJS v8 version of @pixi/graphics-smooth?

`@pixi/graphics-smooth` targets PixiJS v7, and its 1.1 line needs PixiJS 7.2 or a newer v7. SilkGraphics has a v8-style `fill()` and `stroke()` API.
